api/Egap.Documents.WordCompatibility.htm.title: Class WordCompatibility | Egap
api/Egap.Documents.WordCompatibility.htm.summary: Class WordCompatibility Namespace Egap.Documents Assembly Egap.Documents.dll Word's compatibility options that change how Egap lays a document out, one named flag each (Word's w:compat settings). A flag's value is the one the file or code set, else the default for the document's CompatibilityMode, so changing the mode changes every flag nobody set. Word's other compatibility options are read too, kept for round trips and listed in OtherSettings. public sealed class WordCompatibility Inheritance object WordCompatibility Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A new document has Word 2013's settings: OverrideTableStyleFontSizeAndJustification and EnableOpenTypeFeatures on, and Word's doNotFlipMirrorIndents and differentiateMultirowTableHeaders in OtherSettings. A DOCX file's flags are what its settings part says; a flag the file does not set is off, as ECMA-376 and Word's own extensions define it. Properties AllowSpaceOfSameStyleInTable Contextual spacing (ContextualSpacing) is ignored in table cells, so paragraphs of the same style there keep their space (Word's allowSpaceOfSameStyleInTable). public bool AllowSpaceOfSameStyleInTable { get; set; } Property Value bool AllowTextAfterFloatingTableBreak Text may follow a floating table on the page where the table breaks (Word's allowTextAfterFloatingTableBreak). public bool AllowTextAfterFloatingTableBreak { get; set; } Property Value bool DoNotBreakWrappedTables A floating table is kept on one page instead of continuing on the next (Word's doNotBreakWrappedTables). public bool DoNotBreakWrappedTables { get; set; } Property Value bool DoNotUseIndentAsNumberingTabStop A hanging indent is not a tab stop for the tab after a list label, which then goes to the next tab stop (Word's doNotUseIndentAsNumberingTabStop). public bool DoNotUseIndentAsNumberingTabStop { get; set; } Property Value bool EnableOpenTypeFeatures The OpenType features runs ask for (Features: ligatures, contextual alternates, stylistic sets, number forms and spacing) are used. When off, as in files older than Word 2010, text is shaped without them (Word's enableOpenTypeFeatures); kerning (Kerning) still applies. public bool EnableOpenTypeFeatures { get; set; } Property Value bool OtherSettings Word's compatibility options read from the file that Egap keeps but does not act on, by name: a w:compat child's local name with its value (1 when on), or a w:compatSetting's name with its val. public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> OtherSettings { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> OverrideTableStyleFontSizeAndJustification A table style's font size and alignment win over the default paragraph style's, as the style hierarchy says. When off, as in files older than Word 2010, a default paragraph style of 11 or 12 points leaves table text at the table style's size, and a left-aligned default paragraph style leaves it at the table style's alignment (Word's overrideTableStyleFontSizeAndJustification). public bool OverrideTableStyleFontSizeAndJustification { get; set; } Property Value bool SplitPageBreakAndParagraphMark The paragraph mark after a page break that ends a paragraph moves to the next page and takes a line there, as before Word 2013 (Word's splitPgBreakAndParaMark). public bool SplitPageBreakAndParagraphMark { get; set; } Property Value bool TableIndentFromCellText A left-aligned table's indent is measured to its first cell's text, so the table's edge sits the cell's left margin further left. Word has no setting of its own for this: it is on below compatibility mode 15 (Word 2013), and a value set here is not saved to DOCX. public bool TableIndentFromCellText { get; set; } Property Value bool Methods UseModeDefaults() Forgets every flag value the file or code set, so each flag follows CompatibilityMode. public void UseModeDefaults()

api/Egap.Documents.html.title: Namespace Egap.Documents | Egap
api/Egap.Documents.html.summary: Namespace Egap.Documents Classes Block A node that goes into a story or a table cell: a paragraph or a table. Content controls and kept islands join in Build Plan task 5. BlockContainer A node that holds blocks: a story (body, header, footer) or a table cell. BlockIsland A block kept whole, such as an embedded document part (Word's altChunk), as raw markup. Body A section's main text. Bookmark A bookmark found in a document: its start, its end if any, and the text between. BookmarkEnd The end of a bookmark range. BookmarkStart The start of a bookmark: a named place, or a named range up to the BookmarkEnd of the same name. Border One border line: style, width and colour, the space between it and the text, and Word's shadow and frame flags. BoxShadow A shadow a box casts (CSS box-shadow): the box's shape moved by the offsets, grown by Spread and blurred by Blur, drawn behind the box. BoxStyle How a box is drawn around its content: margins, padding, borders, background, rounded corners and a shadow, and the size it asks for. Flex and grid containers and their items, and groups of blocks (Box), take one. Immutable; set a new one to change the box. Break A line, page or column break inside a paragraph. Cell A table cell: blocks, nested tables included. Word wants at least one paragraph in every cell; the model allows none, and writers add the paragraph where the format needs it. CellFormat Table cell formatting: width, merges, vertical alignment, margins, borders and shading. Every property is nullable: null means not set here. CharacterStyle A character style: character formatting for runs. Comment A comment: its reference mark in the text, holding the comment's own text, author and date (Phase 6 design Q8). The text it is about lies between a CommentRangeStart and CommentRangeEnd with its Id. A reply names the comment it answers in ParentId, as Word does. CommentRangeEnd The end of the text a Comment is about; it pairs with the comment by CommentId. CommentRangeStart The start of the text a Comment is about; it pairs with the comment by CommentId. CommentStory The text of a comment. CompositeInline An inline that holds other inlines: a hyperlink or an inline content control. ContentControl A content control around blocks: paragraphs, tables and other controls. ContentControlProperties The settings content controls have, block or inline: kind, tag, title, locks and placeholder state. ControlChar The characters GetText() uses for what is not text, as Word's own text ranges do. ConversionWarning One kind of thing a writer left out, with how many times it happened. DoclingImage A picture's image for ImageResolver. DoclingJson Layout as DoclingDocument JSON (design Q14, Build Plan task 18), the format Docling writes, schema version SchemaVersion: texts, tables, pictures and list groups in flat arrays, linked into reading order from the body by JSON pointers; roles as Docling's labels; bounds as provenance with the page number and a box from the page's bottom left, as PDF measures; page headers and footers in the furniture layer; and Egap's role and confidence in each item's meta. A DoclingDocument from Docling reads back into page layouts. DoclingJsonOptions How DoclingJson writes. Document A flow document: a list of sections, each with its page setup, body and headers and footers, holding paragraphs, tables and the rest of the model (Phase 6 design Q3). The root of the tree; every other node belongs to exactly one document. DocumentBuilder Barcodes. DocumentChangedEventArgs One change to a document (Phase 6 design Q3, editor-ready model): the node, what happened to it and where. Code that keeps a view of the document, such as another library's editor or a cache, redraws from these; undo and redo can be built on them too. DocumentException A file could not be read as the format it was given as: not a package, a part missing or malformed beyond repair. DocumentLimitException A file went past one of the reader's limits (Phase 6 design Q9: part sizes, entry counts, compression ratio, nesting), so reading stopped instead of using unbounded memory or time. The limits are in the format's load options. DocumentLimits The limits a reader keeps to on untrusted files; the defaults suit any real document. DocumentPreview Sends a document's pages to the egap-preview tool (dotnet tool install -g Egap.Preview), which shows them on a local web page and shows them again each time new pages arrive: run the code under dotnet watch and the page follows every edit. DocumentProperties A document's properties: the core ones every format knows (title, author, dates) and custom ones by name, which fields such as TITLE, AUTHOR and DOCPROPERTY show. DocumentSettings Document-wide settings that change layout and numbering: the default tab stop, odd and even headers, footnote and endnote numbering, change tracking and Word's compatibility mode and options. Word's other settings are kept by the DOCX reader as extension data on the document. DocumentVisitor Walks a document tree through Accept(DocumentVisitor): a start and an end method for each node that holds others, one method for each inline. Override the ones you need; the rest continue. The walk does not recurse, so deeply nested tables cannot overflow the stack. DocxFormat Word's DOCX format, with its DOTX and DOCM variants (Phase 6 design Q9 and Q10): strict and transitional files read into the model, with what the model does not name kept as extension data so a DOCX round trip keeps it. DocxLoadOptions How DocxFormat reads a file. DocxSaveOptions How DocxFormat writes a file. EmbeddedFont A font file a document carries (Phase 6 design Q10 and Q12): the layout engine looks here first for a family's face. EpubFormat EPUB books read into the model and written from it: EPUB 2.0.1 and 3.0 to 3.3 read as one document with a section per chapter, the table of contents as outline levels and the metadata as document properties; the model written as an EPUB 3.3 book with a navigation document, an EPUB 2 table of contents for older readers, and accessibility metadata. Books under DRM are refused. EpubLoadOptions How an EPUB book is read. EpubSaveOptions How the model is written as an EPUB 3.3 book. ExtensionData What a format's reader found on a node that the model does not name, kept so the same format's writer can put it back (Phase 6 design Q7): for DOCX, unknown elements and attributes as raw XML with their place among the mapped children. Each format keeps its own data under its name ("docx", "html"); writers of other formats leave it alone. An edit that removes a node removes its data with it. Field A field as a whole: its start, separator and end and the nodes between them. The code is the text between the start and the separator (or the end); the result is between the separator and the end. Fields nest, as in Word. FieldEnd The end of a field (Word's fldChar end). FieldSeparator The separator between a field's code and its result (Word's fldChar separate). FieldStart The start of a field (Word's fldChar begin). A field is a start, its code (runs), an optional separator, its result (runs, maybe over several paragraphs) and an end; GetField() gathers them. FindOptions How Find(string, FindOptions?) and Replace(string, string, FindOptions?) match. FlexContainer A flex container (CSS flexbox): items laid out in a row or a column, growing and shrinking to share the space, wrapped onto more lines when they ask for it. The page flow breaks between lines; DOCX writes the container as a borderless table. FlexItem An item of a FlexContainer: blocks laid out in a box that grows and shrinks with the line. FlexLayout How a flex container lays out its items (CSS flexbox): direction, wrapping, how the space left on a line is shared and how items line up across it, and the gaps between items and lines. Immutable; set a new one to change it. FloatingPlacement Where a floating picture, shape or text box sits and how text wraps around it (Word's anchor): position by alignment or offset from a reference area, wrap mode and side, the distances text keeps, and the stacking order. Immutable; set a new one to move the object. FontFeatures OpenType features turned on or off for some text, such as liga=0 for no standard ligatures or tnum for tabular figures. A feature's value is 1 for on, 0 for off, or a number for features that choose among alternates. The set is compared by value, so two runs with the same features share formatting. Footnote A footnote or endnote: the reference mark in the text, which holds the note's own text as a story (Phase 6 design Q8). The mark is numbered automatically unless it has a CustomMark. FormatBase A set of formatting properties as Word keeps them (Phase 6 design Q5): every property is nullable, and null means "not set here", so the value comes from the style, the document defaults or the application. The format of a node or style reports each change to its document; a format made with new stands alone, for passing to the methods that copy it. FormatRevision A tracked formatting change: who changed the formatting, when, and what it was before. FramePosition An old-style text frame (Word's w:framePr): the paragraph, with the paragraphs after it that have the same frame, is placed as a float by its anchors and alignment, and is never split across pages. A frame with a DropCap is a drop cap: its text sits at the start of the next paragraph, which wraps beside it. Immutable. GridContainer A grid container (CSS grid): items placed in cells of column and row tracks, by line, by named area or automatically, and spanning several. The page flow breaks between rows; DOCX writes the container as a borderless table. GridItem An item of a GridContainer: blocks in a box placed in one cell or spanning several. A line number counts from 1 at the grid's start, and from -1 at the end of the explicit grid; null leaves the item to automatic placement. GridLayout How a grid container lays out its items (CSS grid): the column and row tracks, the size of tracks it adds, named areas, automatic placement, gaps and alignment. Immutable; set a new one to change it. GroupPaging How a group of blocks (a block content control) is placed across pages. Word keeps the blocks but not these settings, which only Egap's layout follows. HeaderFooter A section's header or footer of one HeaderFooterKind. HeaderFooterCollection A section's headers and footers: at most one of each kind. HtmlFormat HTML read into the model: parsed by AngleSharp as browsers parse it, styled through Egami.Css's cascade with HTML's default style sheet, and the computed styles mapped onto paragraphs, runs, lists, tables, and flex and grid containers; positioned boxes become floating text boxes. HtmlLoadOptions How HTML is read (Phase 6 design Q14 to Q16). HtmlSaveOptions How the model is written as HTML (Phase 6 design Q16). Hyperlink A hyperlink: the inlines it holds link to an address, a bookmark in the document, or both. ImageData Image bytes as a file stores them, with their media type, such as image/png or image/x-emf. Inline A node that goes into a paragraph: a run of text, a tab or a break. Fields, hyperlinks, bookmarks, notes, comments and drawings join in Build Plan task 5. InlineContentControl A content control around inlines inside a paragraph. Island An inline kept whole (Phase 6 design Q4): a format's raw markup for an equation, chart, SmartArt diagram, OLE object and the like, with the picture the file stores for it, so it survives a round trip and draws as that picture. List A list paragraphs belong to (Word's num): a ListDefinition and, per level, an optional new start or level of its own. Paragraphs join it through SetList(List, int) or their style; ListLabel gives the computed label, such as "3.2.a". ListCollection A document's lists and list definitions (Phase 6 design Q6): Word's numbering part. AddBulleted() and AddNumbered() make a list with Word's default bulleted or numbered levels. ListDefinition A list definition (Word's abstractNum): nine levels with their numbering, labels and indents. Lists (List) use a definition; lists that share one continue each other's numbering unless one restarts. ListLabel A paragraph's computed list label. ListLevel One level of a list definition: where numbering starts, how numbers are written and the label's text, alignment and formatting, and the indents its paragraphs get (Phase 6 design Q6, Word's lvl). ListLevelOverride A change to one level of one list: a new start number, or a whole level of its own (Word's lvlOverride). ListStyle A list style (Word's numbering style): names the list its paragraphs and list definitions follow. MailMergeOptions How a mail merge fills a template. MarginBox Content in one of the page margins, drawn on every page of its section (or only on the first): text such as a title or "Page 3 of 9" with PAGE and NUMPAGES fields, as CSS's @page margin boxes hold. Headers and footers still apply; margin boxes sit beside them and do not move the body. MarginBoxCollection A section's margin boxes: at most one for each position, and one more for each on the first page. MarkdownFormat Reads Markdown into a Document and writes documents as GitHub Flavored Markdown: CommonMark 0.31 with GitHub's tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and footnotes, and YAML front matter, parsed by Markdig. Headings take the Heading 1 to 6 styles, code the HTML Code and HTML Preformatted styles, lists Word list definitions built from their nesting. Writing says in warnings what Markdown cannot hold. MarkdownImage An image the Markdown writer hands to ImageResolver. MarkdownLoadOptions How MarkdownFormat reads Markdown. MarkdownSaveOptions How MarkdownFormat writes Markdown. MergeData Merge data from dictionaries, rows of values with column names, and objects. Node One node of a document tree: the document itself, a section, a story, a block such as a paragraph or table, or an inline such as a run of text. Every node belongs to one Document for its whole life and sits in at most one place in that document's tree; a node made for one document goes into another through Import(Node, bool). NodeCollection<T> The children of one kind a node holds, such as a story's blocks or a paragraph's inlines. The item type keeps wrong children out at compile time (a run cannot go into a story); adding also refuses a node of another document, a node already in the tree and a node that holds the parent. NoteStory The text of a footnote or endnote. PageSetup A section's page setup: paper size, orientation, margins, columns, page numbering and where it starts. Every property is nullable: null means not set here. Paragraph A paragraph: a list of inlines (runs of text, tabs, breaks and the rest) ended by a paragraph mark. ParagraphFormat Paragraph formatting: alignment, indents, spacing, keep rules, tabs, borders and shading (Word's paragraph properties). Every property is nullable: null means not set here. ParagraphStyle A paragraph style: paragraph formatting and the character formatting of its text. Picture A picture in the text: an image of given size, in the line or floating. PreviewOptions Where ShowPreview(Document, PreviewOptions?) sends a document's pages, and how sharp they are drawn. ResolvedParagraphFormat A paragraph's effective formatting (GetEffectiveFormat()): every property with its final value, styles and defaults applied, tab stops added up. Where neither the document nor Word gives a value, Word's defaults apply. ResolvedRunFormat A run's effective formatting (GetEffectiveFormat()): every property with its final value, styles and defaults applied, theme fonts named. Where neither the document nor Word gives a value, Word's own defaults apply (10 pt, Times New Roman, automatic colour). Revision A tracked insertion, deletion or move on a node: what, who and when. Row A table row: its cells in order. RowFormat Table row formatting: height, header repeat and page splitting. Every property is nullable: null means not set here. Run A run of text with one formatting (Build Plan task 3). RunFormat Character formatting: font, size, colour, bold and the rest (Word's run properties). Every property is nullable: null means not set here. Section A part of a document with its own page setup (Build Plan task 3), a body and up to three headers and three footers (first page, odd or every page, even pages). Shading Shading behind text, a paragraph or a cell: a fill colour, a pattern and the pattern's colour. Shape A shape in the text, in the line or floating, with a fill and an outline, and optionally text inside it (a text box, Phase 6 design Q11). Story Content that flows on its own: a section's body or a header or footer. Footnotes, comments and text boxes join in Build Plan task 5. Style A named set of formatting that paragraphs, runs or tables point at, as in Word (Phase 6 design Q5). A style can be based on another of the same type, taking every property it does not set from it. Styles belong to one document's StyleCollection. StyleCollection A document's styles, by id, with the document defaults every style builds on (Word's docDefaults). A new document has Word's Normal paragraph style, Default Paragraph Font and Normal Table, with Word 2013+'s defaults (11 pt body font from the theme, 8 pt after paragraphs, 1.08 line spacing); AddBuiltIn(BuiltInStyle) adds the others Word knows, such as headings. Tab A tab: the text moves on to the paragraph's next tab stop. TabStop A tab stop: where, how text lines up, and the leader. Table A table: rows of cells, each cell holding blocks, so tables nest. Rows need not have the same number of cells; merged cells and widths come with the table format in Build Plan task 3. TableFormat Table formatting: width, alignment, layout, default cell margins, borders, shading and style options. Every property is nullable: null means not set here. TablePosition Where a floating table sits and how text keeps clear of it (Word's w:tblpPr and w:tblOverlap). A table with a position is laid out as a float that text wraps around on the side with more room, and continues on the next page when it does not fit. Immutable; set a new one to move the table. TableStyle A table style: formatting for the whole table and, apart, for its first and last rows and columns, bands and corners. TableStyleConditional The formatting a table style gives one TableStyleRegion. TextBoxStory The text inside a text box. TextColumn One text column of a section with unequal columns: its width and the space after it, in points. TextFormat Plain text read line by line into paragraphs, and the document written as plain text in reading order, for search and indexing (Phase 6 Build Plan task 8c): one line per paragraph, list labels before their text with a tab, table rows as tab-separated cells, text boxes after the paragraph they are anchored in, equations as their text. Field codes, deleted and hidden text, comments and pictures are left out. TextMatch A match Find(string, FindOptions?) found: where it is in its paragraph's text as Find sees it (runs joined, a tab as \t, a line break as \v, deleted text left out unless the options keep it) and the text it matched. TextSaveOptions How TextFormat writes plain text. Theme A document theme: twelve colours and the major (headings) and minor (body) fonts, which runs and styles name instead of fixed values, so changing the theme restyles the document. A new document has Word's Office theme (2013 to 2022). ThemeColors A theme's twelve colours. TrackedChange One tracked change in a document (Phase 6 design Q8): a Revision or FormatRevision on a node, which can be accepted or rejected on its own. TrackedChangeCollection A document's tracked changes in document order, to read, accept or reject. WordCompatibility Word's compatibility options that change how Egap lays a document out, one named flag each (Word's w:compat settings). A flag's value is the one the file or code set, else the default for the document's CompatibilityMode, so changing the mode changes every flag nobody set. Word's other compatibility options are read too, kept for round trips and listed in OtherSettings. Structs BoxCorners The radius of each corner of a box, in points; 0 for a square corner. DocumentColor A colour as documents give it: automatic, a fixed colour, or a theme colour with Word's tint (towards white) or shade (towards black), so a theme change recolours the text that uses it. The default value is automatic. GridTrack A grid column or row: its least and greatest size (CSS minmax). A single size is both, except a fraction, which grows from its content's size as CSS's 1fr does. GridTrackSize One limit of a grid track's size: a length, a share of the space, or a size from the content. TableWidth A table or cell width: automatic, in points or in per cent. Interfaces IMergeData One record of data for a mail merge: the value of each merge field, and the records of each repeated region. Implement it to stream records from any source; MergeData makes one from dictionaries, rows or objects. Enums BorderStyle A line style for borders, as Word's border types without the art borders (kept by the DOCX reader as extension data). BreakKind What a Break ends. BuiltInStyle Styles Word knows by name, which AddBuiltIn(BuiltInStyle) adds with Word 2013+'s definitions. ContentControlKind What kind of content control (Word's structured document tag) it is. ConversionWarningKind What a reader or writer had to leave out or change because a format cannot hold it. DoclingImageMode How DoclingJson writes pictures' images. DocumentChangeKind What happened in a Changed notification. DocumentColorKind How a DocumentColor is given. DocumentFormatKind The kind of file Identify(Stream, string?) finds, without loading it. DocxKind Which of Word's file kinds a DOCX package is (Phase 6 design Q10). DropCap A paragraph frame's drop cap kind (Word's w:dropCap). EpubSplit Where the EPUB writer starts a new chapter file. FieldKind The kind of a field, from the first word of its code. Fields Egap does not know are Unknown and keep their stored result (Phase 6 design Q8). FlexDirection Which way a flex container lays its items out. FlexWrap Whether a flex container's items go on more lines when they do not fit on one. FloatingAlignment Where a floating object lines up within what it is measured from, instead of an offset. FrameWrap How text wraps around a paragraph frame (Word's w:framePr w:wrap). GridAutoFlow Which way a grid's automatic placement fills cells, and whether it goes back to fill holes. GridTrackUnit What a grid track size is given in. HeaderFooterKind Which pages a header or footer is for. HighlightColor Text highlighting colours, the sixteen Word offers. HorizontalAnchor What a floating object's horizontal position is measured from. IslandKind What a kept island holds (Phase 6 design Q4): content the model keeps whole, as raw markup, drawn as its picture. KashidaLevel How far a justified paragraph's Arabic lines are stretched with tatweels (kashida) between letters, as Word's low, medium and high kashida alignments; the rest of a line's free width goes to word spaces. Scripts without kashida justify at spaces. LayoutAlignment How boxes line up along a container's axis: flex and grid containers and their items use the same values. Each property says which values it takes, as CSS gives each its own set; a value a property does not take lines up as Start. LineSpacingRule How LineSpacing is read. ListKind How a list definition's levels are meant to be used, as Word records it. ListLabelSuffix What follows a list label before the paragraph's text. MarginBoxPosition Where a MarginBox sits in the page margins: the sixteen boxes of CSS Paged Media, three along each edge and one in each corner. MarkdownExtensions The Markdown extensions the reader understands beyond CommonMark (Phase 6 design Q17). MarkdownImageMode What the Markdown writer does with pictures that have no address of their own. NoteKind Whether a note is a footnote or an endnote. NumberStyle How page numbers are written. PageOrientation Page orientation. ParagraphAlignment How a paragraph's lines line up between its indents. RevisionKind What a tracked change did (Phase 6 design Q8: changes are marks on the nodes they change). RowHeightRule How a row's height is read. SectionStart Where a section starts. ShadingPattern A shading pattern: Word's set, from clear (fill only) to solid (pattern colour only) by percentages and hatches. ShapeKind The shape a Shape draws (Word's preset geometry), from the common ones. StyleType The kind of a Style. TabAlignment How text lines up at a tab stop. TabLeader What fills the space before a tab stop. TableAlignment Where a table sits between the margins. TableLayoutKind How a table's column widths are found. TableStyleRegion The parts of a table a table style can format apart (Word's conditional formatting). TextDirection Which way text runs in a cell or section. ThemeColor Which of a theme's twelve colours a DocumentColor names, as Word's themes have them. ThemeFont Which theme font a run's font slot names. TrackedChangeTarget What part of a node a TrackedChange is about. UnderlineStyle How text is underlined, as Word's underline types. VerticalAlignment Where content sits vertically in a cell, or a page's text in a section. VerticalAnchor What a floating object's vertical position is measured from. VerticalMerge A cell's part in a vertical merge. VerticalTextPosition Raised or lowered text. VisitorAction What a DocumentVisitor wants the walk to do next. WidthUnit How a table, cell or row width or height is given. WordBreak Where lines may break inside words. WrapMode How text flows around a floating object (Phase 6 design Q11: all six of Word's wrap modes). WrapSide Which sides of a floating object text flows on.

api/Egap.Pdf.Ocr.PdfOcr.html.summary: Class PdfOcr Namespace Egap.Pdf.Ocr Assembly Egap.Pdf.dll Makes scanned PDFs searchable through any OCR engine (an Egami.Ocr.IOcrEngine from Egami.Ocr): each page's image goes to the engine, and the words that come back are written over the page as invisible text, placed and scaled so selection follows the scan. Egap ships no engine; plug in Egami.Ocr.CommandOcrEngine for a program such as Tesseract, or your own class around an OS or cloud service. public static class PdfOcr Inheritance object PdfOcr Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("scan.pdf"); CommandOcrEngine tesseract = new("tesseract {image} {output} -l {langs} --dpi {dpi} hocr", new CommandOcrOptions { Output = OcrOutputFormat.Hocr }); PdfOcrReport report = await PdfOcr.MakeSearchableAsync(pdf, tesseract, new PdfOcrOptions { PdfA = PdfAConformance.PdfA2b }); pdf.Save("searchable.pdf"); Remarks The document is changed in place and saved by the caller. A page that is one scanned image is read as its own pixels; other pages are rendered. Pages go to the engine several at a time when it is thread-safe. A signed document is refused unless AllowInvalidatingSignatures. Methods MakeSearchableAsync(PdfDocument, IOcrEngine, PdfOcrOptions?, CancellationToken) Recognizes the text of a document's pages and adds it as an invisible layer. public static Task<PdfOcrReport> MakeSearchableAsync(PdfDocument document, IOcrEngine engine, PdfOcrOptions? options = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters document PdfDocument The document, changed in place. engine IOcrEngine The OCR engine. options PdfOcrOptions Which pages, how and with what limits; Default when null. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels the run; pages already done keep their text. Returns Task<PdfOcrReport> What happened to each page. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A page in Pages is not in the document. PdfLimitException More pages than MaxPages. PdfException The document is signed and AllowInvalidatingSignatures is not set.

Malformed = 1 The /ByteRange is missing, has an odd count, or holds something other than offsets and lengths. None = 0 The byte range is well formed. api/Egap.Pdf.PdfWarningCode.html.title: Enum PdfWarningCode | Egap
api/Egap.Pdf.PdfWarningCode.html.summary: Enum PdfWarningCode Namespace Egap.Pdf Assembly Egap.Pdf.dll What kind of repair a PdfWarning records. public enum PdfWarningCode Fields AppearanceNotDrawn = 32 An appearance stream was not drawn, such as for text the standard 14 fonts cannot show; the annotation or field keeps the appearance it had. BrokenXrefChain = 21 A /Prev or /XRefStm pointed nowhere useful or back into the chain; older sections were not read. DamagedFilterData = 18 A stream's encoded data was damaged; what decoded before the damage was kept. DuplicateKey = 12 A dictionary had the same key twice; the last value was kept. FieldRenamed = 34 An imported form field was renamed with a suffix, since the document has a field of that name (Phase 2 Q5). FontProgramUnreadable = 40 A font's embedded program could not be read as TrueType, OpenType, CFF or Type 1; the font's metrics and text still work, but not its outlines. InvalidReference = 13 A reference had an object number below 1 or a generation above 65,535; it was read as null. MalformedContent = 36 A content stream held something that is not an operation (stray delimiters, operands with no operator after them, an unclosed array, a stream that could not be decoded); it was skipped or closed and reading went on. MalformedDictionary = 11 A dictionary key was not a name, or a key had no value; the entry was dropped. MalformedEncryption = 28 Encrypted data or the encryption dictionary was malformed; it was read as far as it made sense. MalformedFilterParameters = 19 A filter's /DecodeParms held values out of range; the filter ran with its defaults or without a predictor. MalformedHexString = 5 A hex string held a character that is not a hex digit or white space, or had no closing >. MalformedInlineImage = 38 An inline image's end (EI) could not be found where its length or filters put it; it was found by searching, or the image runs to the end of the content. MalformedName = 3 A name had a # not followed by two hex digits; the # was kept as is. MalformedNumber = 1 A number was malformed (such as --5, 1.2.3 or 4-2) and was read the way other readers do. MalformedObjectStream = 22 An object stream's header or offsets were malformed; the objects that could be found were kept. MalformedOutline = 31 The outline was malformed (chains of items that loop or reach something that is not an item, or a wrong /Parent, /Prev or /Last); it was repaired in memory. MalformedPageTree = 30 The page tree was malformed (kids that are not dictionaries or loop back, a wrong /Type, /Parent or /Count, or no tree at all); it was repaired in memory. MalformedStreamKeyword = 15 The stream keyword was not followed by a line feed or carriage return and line feed. MalformedTree = 29 A name tree or number tree was malformed (its nodes loop, its limits or entries are missing, wrong or out of order); it was read as far as it made sense, and rebuilt from its entries when edited. MalformedXref = 20 A cross-reference table or stream was malformed (wrong counts, bad entries, numbering off by one); it was read as far as it made sense. MissingEndobj = 14 An indirect object had no endobj. MissingEndstream = 17 A stream had no endstream; its data was taken to run to endobj or the end of the file. MissingHeader = 24 The file has no %PDF-n.n header in its first kilobyte; version 1.7 was assumed. MissingObject = 23 An object was not where the cross-reference said, or had another number or generation, or could not be loaded; the reference was read as null. MissingSeparator = 7 Two tokens were run together with no white space or delimiter between them. NotImported = 33 Part of a source document was not brought along with imported pages, such as its structure tree (tagged PDF comes in 5.x) or its XFA form. NumberOutOfRange = 2 An integer was too large for 64 bits and was read as a real number. ObjectRelocated = 27 An object was not at the offset the cross-reference gave; it was found nearby or by scanning the file. PageReferencesRemoved = 35 A removed page's outline destinations, links or named destinations were cleaned up (Phase 2 Q7); the message gives the counts. RasterFallback = 39 A PdfCanvas call that PDF cannot express (a blur, noise, a Porter-Duff blend, a layer filter) was drawn into an image at the fallback resolution and placed instead (Phase 3 design Q14). ShiftedOffsets = 25 The header was not at the start of the file, and the file's offsets count from the header; they were read that way. SignatureInvalidated = 42 A save or a new signature changes the document in a way an existing signature does not allow, or rewrites a signed file whole, so that signature no longer verifies (Phase 5 design Q7); in strict mode it throws instead, and AllowInvalidatingSignatures or AllowInvalidatingSignatures lets it go ahead. TextNotReplaced = 43 A match of ReplaceText(string, string, PdfFindOptions?, PdfReplaceOptions?) was left as it was: its font lacks a glyph the new text needs, or its text cannot be written in that font, and no fallback font was given; or the match is a marked-content span's replacement text (/ActualText), not glyphs. TextWithoutUnicode = 41 Text extraction found glyphs whose fonts say no Unicode text for them (no ToUnicode map, no glyph name the Adobe Glyph List knows); they were given private-use characters (Phase 3 design Q10). TooManyWarnings = 8 The file had so many warnings that the rest were dropped. UnexpectedDelimiter = 6 A stray delimiter () or a single >) was skipped. UnexpectedToken = 9 A token that cannot appear where it was found, such as an unknown keyword or a stray ], was skipped. UnterminatedObject = 10 An array or dictionary was not closed; it was closed where the object ended. UnterminatedString = 4 A literal string ran to the end of the data without its closing parenthesis. WrongOperandCount = 37 An operator had more or fewer operands than the spec gives it; the operation was kept as written. WrongStreamLength = 16 A stream's /Length was missing or wrong; its data was found by searching for endstream. XrefRebuilt = 26 The cross-reference could not be used, or named no catalog; it was rebuilt by scanning the file for objects.

api/Egap.Pdf.PdfXConverter.html.summary: Class PdfXConverter Namespace Egap.Pdf Assembly Egap.Pdf.dll Checks documents against PDF/X and converts them to it (Phase 8 design Q9, Q10). PDF/X-4 and X-6 are checked and converted; X-1a and X-3 too when the file has no transparency, which conversion does not flatten; X-4p, X-5g, X-5pg and X-6p are checked only; X-5n and X-6n are checked, with an n-colorant output intent. Conversion fixes in place what it can (output intent, trim and bleed boxes, identification and metadata, trapping key, fonts, colours through PdfColorConverter, transfer functions, annotations in the print area, actions) and reports every fix; when a rule cannot be met nothing is changed. Issues are PdfAIssues, as for PDF/A. No open validator judges PDF/X: Acrobat Preflight or PackzView is the full judge. public static class PdfXConverter Inheritance object PdfXConverter Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("brochure.pdf"); PdfAReport report = PdfXConverter.Convert(pdf, PdfXConformance.PdfX4, new PdfXConvertOptions { OutputCondition = PdfOutputCondition.Fogra39, Bleed = 3 }); if (report.Succeeded) { pdf.Save("print.pdf"); } Methods Check(PdfDocument, PdfXConformance, CancellationToken) Checks a document against conformance's rules, changing nothing; each issue says whether conversion can fix it. public static PdfAReport Check(PdfDocument document, PdfXConformance conformance, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters document PdfDocument conformance PdfXConformance cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns PdfAReport Exceptions ArgumentException conformance is None.
