api/Egap.Pdf.html.title: Namespace Egap.Pdf | Egap
api/Egap.Pdf.html.summary: Namespace Egap.Pdf Classes BlankPageOptions When RemoveBlankPages(BlankPageOptions?, CancellationToken) takes a page for blank (Phase 7 design Q15). BookletOptions How Booklet(PdfDocument, BookletOptions?) lays a saddle-stitched booklet out. DeskewOptions How DeskewScannedPages(DeskewOptions?, CancellationToken) straightens scans. GridOptions How Grid(PdfDocument, GridOptions?) puts every page on one sheet. NUpOptions How NUp(PdfDocument, NUpOptions?) lays pages out (Phase 7 design Q9). PdfAConvertOptions Options for Convert(PdfDocument, PdfAConformance, PdfAConvertOptions?). PdfAConverter Converts documents to PDF/A and checks them against the rules Egap enforces (Phase 5 design Q12, Q13). Conversion keeps the file's objects and fixes what it can, reporting every fix; if any rule cannot be met, nothing is changed. A converted document saves by the part's rules from then on: written whole, without encryption, as the part's version. PdfAIssue One PDF/A rule a document broke (Phase 5 design Q12, Q13), and whether conversion can put it right or did. PdfAReport What a PDF/A conversion did or a check found (Phase 5 design Q12, Q13). A conversion that could not meet every rule changed nothing; its report lists every issue, the ones it would have fixed with Fixable set. PdfAction An action (12.6): a thin view over its dictionary, typed by /S through FromDictionary(PdfDictionary). JavaScript and any action type Egap does not know are plain PdfActions: kept and written back as they are, never run. Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary. PdfAnnotation An annotation (12.5): a thin view over its dictionary, typed by /Subtype through FromDictionary(PdfDictionary) (Phase 2 Q10). Subtypes Egap has no class for (Sound, Movie, Screen, 3D, RichMedia, PrinterMark, TrapNet, Watermark, Projection and any unknown one) are plain PdfAnnotations, read and written through Dictionary. Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary. PdfAnnotationCollection A page's annotations (12.5): its /Annots array, in order, each annotation once. Entries that are not dictionaries are left out, as pdf.js and PDFium leave them out. Adding and removing edit the array in place, keep each annotation's /P pointing at the page, and keep popups with the annotations they belong to. PdfArray A PDF array. PdfAttachment An embedded file (7.11.4): a thin view over its file specification dictionary, which holds the embedded file stream in /EF. Two views are equal when they wrap the same file specification. PdfAttachmentCollection The document's embedded files (7.11.4): the catalog's /Names /EmbeddedFiles name tree, in key order. Adding and removing edit the tree in place (Phase 2 Q3) and keep the catalog's /AF associated files (PDF 2.0) in step. PdfBatesSequence A Bates numbering sequence (Phase 7 design Q11): numbers with a prefix, a suffix and a fixed number of digits, continuing across every document stamped with it, so a set of documents is numbered page by page from one start. PdfBoolean A PDF boolean. There are two instances, True and False. PdfButtonOptions How a new check box or radio group works. PdfCanvas An Egami canvas that draws onto a PDF page: the same drawing code that fills a raster writes PDF operators here (Phase 3, hub Q10). Paths, strokes, clips, opacity and blend modes become vector content; what PDF cannot express is drawn into an image at FallbackDpi and placed instead, with a warning. PdfCanvasOptions How a PdfCanvas draws onto a page. PdfCaretAnnotation A caret annotation (12.5.6.11, PDF 1.5): marks where text is to be inserted. PdfCertificateSeed Certificate constraints of a seed value (/Cert, ISO 32000-2, Table 238). PdfCheckBoxField A check box (12.7.5.2.3): on or off. PdfChoiceField A choice field (12.7.5.4): a combo box or list box of options. PdfChoiceFieldOptions How a new combo box or list box works. PdfCircleAnnotation A circle annotation (12.5.6.8): an ellipse drawn inside the annotation's rectangle. PdfClipPath A clip the content set (8.5.4): a path, the transformation it was set under, and its fill rule. PdfColor A colour as content sets it (8.6): its colour space, as named in the content and resolved through the resources (a name such as DeviceRGB, or an array such as [/ICCBased 7 0 R]), its components, and for a pattern the pattern's resource name. PdfColorConversionOptions How Convert(PdfDocument, PdfColorConversionOptions?, CancellationToken) converts a document. PdfColorConversionResult What a colour conversion changed. PdfColorConverter Converts a document's colours into a print profile (Phase 8 design Q6 to Q8): RGB, calibrated, Lab and ICC-based colours go to the target, CMYK and spot colours stay unless the options say otherwise, and vectors stay vectors. Colour operators, images, shadings, patterns, soft masks, Type 3 glyphs, annotation appearances and spot alternates are all converted. Ink coverage is not limited: the target profile sets it, and preflight reports anything over a print profile's limit. PdfComboBoxField A combo box (12.7.5.4): a drop-down list, editable or not. PdfCompare Compares two PDF documents (Phase 7 design 7.4): a text pass that diffs the words of both documents in reading order and matches pages by the words they share, and a visual pass that renders each matching pair of pages and boxes the pixels that differ. Both documents must stay open while the comparison is used, as markup reads the new one. PdfCompareOptions How Run(PdfDocument, PdfDocument, PdfCompareOptions?, CancellationToken) compares two documents (Phase 7 design Q12 and Q13). PdfComparedWord A word compare read, with the page (1-based) and box (default user space) it is on. PdfComparison What changed between two documents (Phase 7 design Q12 and Q13): text changes found by a word-level diff over the whole documents, so text that only moved to another page is no change; how pages match; and where matching pages render differently. WriteMarkup(string) writes a copy of the new document with the changes marked. PdfContent The operations of a content stream (8.2): a page's content, a form XObject's, a Type 3 glyph's, or content built from scratch. It is a plain list (Phase 3 design Q3): operations can be read, inserted, removed and replaced, and operators the spec does not define are kept, so content round-trips whatever it holds. PdfContentWalker Walks content with its resources and tracks the graphics state (8.4) through it: the transformation matrix, q and Q, the text state and matrices, colours and colour spaces, clips, graphics state dictionaries and marked content. It descends into form XObjects and Type 3 glyph procedures. Derive from it and override the On methods to see paths, glyphs, images, shadings and marked content with the state they are drawn in (Phase 3 design Q3). PdfContentWriter Writes a content stream (8.2) operator by operator, every operator of ISO 32000-2 table A.1 included, into bytes for a page, form XObject or appearance stream. Operands are written as the object writer writes objects, so names and strings are escaped, and numbers have no exponents: whole numbers as integers, others rounded to five decimals, or to six significant digits below 1. Saves, text objects and marked content are counted, and ToArray() refuses content that leaves one open, which a viewer would misread. PdfCreateOptions Options for Create(PdfCreateOptions). PdfDestination An explicit destination (12.3.2.2): a page and how to show it. The page is a reference to a page of this document, or a page index (from 0) for a destination in another file (PdfGoToRemoteAction). A coordinate or zoom of null leaves the viewer's current value unchanged. PdfDictionary A PDF dictionary: names mapped to objects, kept in the order they were added so a rewrite keeps the file's order. PdfDocument Pages made from images, and pages written as image files. PdfEncryption How a save encrypts the document: keep the encryption it was opened with, drop it, or apply new AES-256 encryption. PdfException The exception thrown when a PDF file cannot be read, or, in strict mode, when it needs any repair. PdfField A form field (12.7.4): a thin view over its field dictionary. Terminal fields are typed by /FT and their flags: PdfTextField, PdfCheckBoxField, PdfRadioButtonField, PdfPushButtonField, PdfComboBoxField, PdfListBoxField and PdfSignatureField; non-terminal fields, and terminal fields of an unknown type, are plain PdfFields. Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary. PdfFieldLock A field lock (ISO 32000-2, 12.7.5.5 and 12.8.2.4): the fields a signature makes read-only, from a signature field's /Lock before signing or from a signature's FieldMDP reference after. PdfFieldOptions What every new form field can have: a tooltip, flags, and how its widget looks. PdfFileAttachmentAnnotation A file attachment annotation (12.5.6.15): a file embedded at a point on the page, shown as an icon. PdfFindOptions How FindText(string, PdfFindOptions?, CancellationToken) and the methods like it search. PdfFont A font a page's text uses (Phase 3 design Q7): read-only. It says what kind of font it is, its names, flags and metrics, how its strings split into codes, each code's width and glyph name, and the text a code stands for, through the font's ToUnicode map first, then its encoding's glyph names through the Adobe Glyph List. Fonts are read leniently: what a file gets wrong gives no answer rather than an exception. PdfFontCollection The fonts a page's resources name (/Font), by resource name: page.Fonts["F1"] is the font /F1 12 Tf selects. Read when asked, so it always shows the resources as they are. PdfForm The interactive form (12.7): a thin view over the catalog's /AcroForm dictionary, whose /Fields are the roots of the field tree. A document without one has no fields. Fields are read leniently: loops, entries that are not dictionaries and trees deeper than 64 levels are skipped, as pdf.js and qpdf skip them. PdfFormXObject A page drawn as a form XObject (Phase 7 design Q8): a whole page that another page can draw, scaled and placed, as imposition and page stamps do. Its space is the page as a viewer shows it: points from the bottom left of the crop box, rotation applied, Width by Height. PdfFreeTextAnnotation A free text annotation (12.5.6.6): text drawn straight on the page, in a box or with a callout line. PdfGoToAction A go-to action (12.6.4.2): goes to a destination in this document, given explicitly or by name. PdfGoToEmbeddedAction An embedded go-to action (12.6.4.4): goes to a destination in an embedded or embedding PDF file. PdfGoToRemoteAction A remote go-to action (12.6.4.3): goes to a destination in another PDF file, whose pages are given by index. PdfGraphicsState The graphics state (8.4) as a PdfContentWalker tracks it: what q saves and Q restores. The text matrices are not in it; they belong to the text object (9.4.2) and are on the walker. PdfHideAction A hide action (12.6.4.10): hides or shows annotations or fields. PdfHighlightAnnotation A highlight annotation (12.5.6.10): text marked as with a highlighter. PdfImage An image a page draws (8.9): an image XObject or an inline image (Phase 3 design Q11). It gives the image's stored bytes and filters, so a JPEG can be saved as it is, and decodes to an Egami raster with its colour space, decode array and masks applied. PdfImageEncoding How Replace(Raster, PdfImageEncoding?) stores a new image. PdfImageOptions How ToRaster(PdfImageOptions?) decodes an image (Phase 3 design Q11 and Q12). PdfImagePageOptions How images become pages in FromImages(IEnumerable<string>, PdfImagePageOptions?). PdfImportOptions Options for importing pages. PdfImpose Imposition (Phase 7 design 7.2, Q9): new documents whose sheets draw the source's pages as form XObjects, placed and scaled. The source is never changed; it must stay open until the result is saved, which reads the pages' streams then. Every layout keeps each page's content, resources and printable annotations, shared once per source. PdfInkAnnotation An ink annotation (12.5.6.13): freehand strokes. PdfInkPlate One ink's plate: its name, whether it is a spot ink, and its raster of how much ink prints where. PdfInlineImage An inline image (8.9.7): BI, its parameters, ID, its data and EI, kept as one operation with the data as stored. Its Operator is BI and it has no operands. PdfInteger A PDF integer, held as 64 bits. PdfInvoice A Factur-X or ZUGFeRD e-invoice in a PDF: the invoice's XML (UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice) attached to a PDF/A-3 document, with the Factur-X schema in the document's XMP saying the file name, the profile and the version. The XML is the invoicing system's to write; Egap embeds it and reads it back. PdfInvoiceOptions How Embed(PdfDocument, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, PdfInvoiceOptions?) embeds an invoice. PdfLaunchAction A launch action (12.6.4.6): opens a file or starts an application. Kept as it is; Egap never launches anything. PdfLayer An optional content group (8.11.2), a layer: a thin view over its dictionary. Its visibility and lock are read from and written to the document's default configuration (/OCProperties /D). Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary. PdfLayerCollection The document's optional content groups (8.11), its layers, from the catalog's /OCProperties /OCGs, each once in the order listed. Removing a layer takes it out of the configurations; the content it marks stays on the pages unless Remove(PdfLayer, bool) is asked to remove it too. PdfLimitException The exception thrown when a file goes past one of the limits in PdfReadOptions. It is never a warning, even outside strict mode: going on could exhaust memory or time. PdfLineAnnotation A line annotation (12.5.6.7): a straight line with optional endings and caption. PdfLinkAnnotation A link annotation (12.5.6.5): an area of the page that goes to a destination or runs an action. PdfListBoxField A list box (12.7.5.4): a scrolling list, with one or several selected. PdfMarkedContent A marked-content sequence or point (14.6): its tag and properties. Properties named in the resources (/OC /MC0 BDC) are looked up there; PropertiesName keeps the name. PdfMarkedContentReference A marked-content sequence a structure element owns: content tagged with an MCID on a page or in a form XObject. PdfMarkupAnnotation A markup annotation (12.5.6.2): one a reader writes on the page, with an author, a popup for its text, and replies. PdfMetadata The document's metadata (14.3) through one API over both stores (Phase 2 Q8): the document information dictionary (/Info in the trailer) and the XMP packet (the catalog's /Metadata stream). Reading prefers XMP when the packet has the property, as pdf.js does. Setting writes the Info entry and, when the document has an XMP packet or is PDF 2.0, the matching XMP property; a document before 2.0 without a packet gets none unless CreateXmp() is called. Setting null removes the property from both. PdfName A PDF name, such as /Type. A name is a sequence of bytes, by convention UTF-8 text; Value is that text without the slash. PdfNamedAction A named action (12.6.4.11), such as NextPage, PrevPage, FirstPage or LastPage. PdfNamedDestinations A document's named destinations (12.3.2.4), found through both lookups: the /Dests name tree in the catalog's /Names (PDF 1.2 and later) and the older /Dests dictionary in the catalog (PDF 1.1). A name in both is taken from the name tree. New names go in the name tree, which is edited in place (Phase 2 Q3). PdfNull The PDF null object. There is one instance, Instance. PdfObject A PDF object (ISO 32000-2, 7.3): PdfBoolean, PdfInteger, PdfReal, PdfString, PdfName, PdfArray, PdfDictionary, PdfStream, PdfNull or a PdfReference to an indirect object. PdfObjectReference An object a structure element owns (an OBJR): an annotation, such as a link or form widget, or an XObject. PdfObjectTable A document's indirect objects, by number. Objects load from the file the first time they are asked for; changing one, anywhere in its tree, marks it as changed, so an incremental save writes only what changed. PdfOcrLayer An invisible text layer over a scanned page (Phase 5 design Q16): the words OCR found, drawn in render mode 3 (neither filled nor stroked) in a glyphless font Egap builds, each word scaled to its box, so the page can be searched, selected and read aloud while it looks exactly as the scan. Words come from hOCR (Tesseract, Kraken, OCRmyPDF) or ALTO (ABBYY, libraries' digitisation) files, or from any OCR engine as word boxes. The page image is not touched. PdfOcrLine A recognised line of words, in reading order. PdfOcrWord A recognised word: its text and its box on the page, in PDF user space (Phase 5 design Q16). PdfOperation One operation of a content stream (8.2): an operator and its operands, such as 1 0 0 1 72 720 cm. Operations are values: they are never changed after they are made, so an edited content stream replaces operations instead of changing them, and the operand objects (arrays and dictionaries included) should be treated as read-only. PdfOptimizeOptions What Optimize(PdfOptimizeOptions?, CancellationToken) does (Phase 7 design Q2 to Q7). A preset fills in the switches; each can be changed with with. Lossless, the default, never changes a pixel: it merges duplicates, subsets fonts, removes what nobody sees, codes bilevel images as CCITT G4, optimizes JPEG Huffman tables and writes object streams. Print, Ebook and Screen also downsample images above 1.5 times their resolution and write photos as JPEG at their quality. PdfOptimizeReport What Optimize(PdfOptimizeOptions?, CancellationToken) did (Phase 7 design 7.1): bytes before and after, by pass, and every image changed. PdfOptimizeSavings What each optimizer pass saved, in stored bytes before the file is written. PdfOptimizedImage One image the optimizer changed. PdfOutline The document outline (bookmarks, 12.3.3), from the catalog's /Outlines. A broken outline (chains that loop, wrong /Prev, /Parent or /Last, kids that are not dictionaries) is repaired in memory on first use with MalformedOutline warnings, as pdf.js and qpdf read it. The outline dictionary is created by the first item added. PdfOutlineItem An outline item (12.3.3): a thin view over its dictionary, equal to another view of the same dictionary. It goes to a destination (/Dest) or runs an action (/A), and has a title, colour, style and open state. PdfOutlineNode A node of the document outline (12.3.3): the outline itself or one of its items. Children are read through /First and /Next; adding, removing and moving keep /First, /Last, /Prev, /Next, /Parent and the /Count of every node above in step, touching only the nodes involved. PdfOutputCondition A registered print characterization (design Q10): the identifier PDF/X output intents name, such as FOGRA39, how it is described, and the ICC profile that is embedded with it. Fogra39 carries Egami's bundled profile; the others need one from the caller (WithProfile(ColorProfile)), since their profiles may not be redistributed freely. PdfPage A page (7.7.3.3): a thin view over the page's dictionary, which it reads and writes directly, so anything it does not cover is still there in Dictionary. Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary (Phase 2 Q1). PdfPageCollection A document's pages in order, numbered from 0 (Phase 2 Q2). The list is built on first use by walking the page tree from the catalog; only the tree's nodes are loaded, not the pages' content. A broken tree is repaired in memory with MalformedPageTree warnings, as pdf.js and PDFium read it. PdfPageLabelRange A range of page labels (12.4.2): from the page at StartIndex (from 0) up to the next range, labels are the prefix followed by a number in the given style, counting from Start. PdfPageMatch Which old page a new page matches; a page only one side has is added or removed. PdfPageRange A choice of pages written as text, such as "1,3,5-10,z", that is turned into page numbers once the page count is known. Pass it to ExtractPages(PdfPageRange), PageRange and the page renderers, or turn it into page indices with Resolve(int) for Import(PdfDocument, IEnumerable<int>?, int?, PdfImportOptions?). PdfPasswordException The exception thrown when an encrypted file needs a password that was not given, or the password given is neither the user nor the owner password. Set Password and open the file again. PdfPath A path as content builds it (8.5.2), in the user space it was built in: subpaths of lines and cubic curves. re becomes a closed subpath of four lines, and v and y become curves with both control points given. PdfPlacedImage An image where a page draws it: the image and the matrix that maps its unit square into the page's default space. PdfPlaceholderValues The values one page's placeholders are filled with, for Fill(string, PdfPlaceholderValues). PdfPlaceholders The placeholders page furniture is written with, the same everywhere Egap fills text per page (stamps, and headers and footers on export): {page}, {total-pages} (also {pages}), {label} (the page label), {date}, {time}, {title} and {file}. PdfPolyLineAnnotation A polyline annotation (12.5.6.9): an open line through its vertices, with optional endings. PdfPolygonAnnotation A polygon annotation (12.5.6.9): a closed shape through its vertices. PdfPopupAnnotation A popup annotation (12.5.6.14): the window that shows a markup annotation's text. PdfPreflight Preflight for print: lists what a document uses and checks it against a PdfPrintProfile. The report shows every output intent, colour space (with its ICC profile and spot names), image resolution, font, transparency, overprint and hairline, page by page, so a file can be shown to hold CMYK under a FOGRA39 intent, or found to carry an RGB photo. Preflight changes nothing. PdfPreflightItem One thing a preflight found in a document: what it is, the page it is on (null for the whole document), a line describing it, and the details that apply to its kind. Uses of the same thing on a page are counted in one item. PdfPreflightReport What Run(PdfDocument, PdfPrintProfile?, CancellationToken) found: every colour space, profile, spot ink, output intent, image resolution, font, transparency, overprint and hairline the document uses, page by page, and the issues that break the print profile it was checked against. Issues are PdfAIssues, as for PDF/A; preflight fixes nothing, so none is fixable. PdfPreparedSignature A signature waiting for its CMS (Phase 5 design Q3): the file is written with the space reserved, and Digest is what a signing service signs. CompleteAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken) writes the CMS it returns into that space, in the same stream; a file prepared earlier, in another process, is completed with CompleteAsync(Stream, ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, PdfTimestampClient?, CancellationToken). PdfPrintProfile What a print job accepts, as Run(PdfDocument, PdfPrintProfile?, CancellationToken) checks it: the most ink, the least image resolution, the colour spaces allowed, the bleed past the trim box, the thinnest rule and whether fonts must be embedded. A preset fills in the values for a common job; each can be changed with with. A value left null is not checked. PdfPushButtonField A push button (12.7.5.2.2): runs an action and has no value. PdfRadioButtonField A radio button group (12.7.5.2.4): one widget per button, at most one on. PdfReadOptions Options for opening a PDF file: the password, strict mode and the limits that protect against hostile files. PdfReal A PDF real number, held as a double. PdfRedactAnnotation A redaction annotation (12.5.6.23, PDF 1.7): marks content to be removed. Applying redactions changes page content, which is layer 3; Phase 2 reads and writes the annotation only. PdfRedactionOptions How redaction annotations are applied (Phase 5 design Q9). PdfRedactionResult What applying redactions removed (Phase 5 design Q9). PdfReference A reference to an indirect object: its object number and generation (12 0 R). References come from the document, from Add(PdfObject) or GetReference(int), so they always resolve through it. PdfRenderOptions How a page is rendered (Phase 4 design Q3 and Q4): the resolution or a size to fit, which box shows, extra rotation, a region of the output for tiles, the intent, the background, annotations and anti-aliasing. The defaults draw the crop box at 72 dpi (one pixel per point) on white with annotations, as a viewer shows the page. PdfReplaceOptions How ReplaceText(string, string, PdfFindOptions?, PdfReplaceOptions?) writes the new text. PdfReplaceResult What ReplaceText(string, string, PdfFindOptions?, PdfReplaceOptions?) did. PdfResetFormAction A reset-form action (12.7.6.3): returns fields to their default values. PdfRevision One revision of a file (Phase 5 design, 5.1): the original file or one incremental update after it (ISO 32000-2, 7.5.6). Each signature covers one revision; verification opens that revision and compares it with the later ones. PdfRevocationSource Where revocation data (OCSP responses and CRLs) comes from (Phase 5 design Q5): Online(HttpClient) asks each certificate's OCSP responder, then its CRL distribution point, through the caller's HttpClient; Offline(IEnumerable<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>?, IEnumerable<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>?) uses responses the caller already has. Egap never opens a connection on its own. PdfSanitizeOptions What Sanitize(PdfSanitizeOptions?) removes (Phase 5 design Q10); every switch is on by default. PdfSanitizeResult What sanitising removed, by kind (Phase 5 design Q10). PdfSaveOptions Options for saving a document. PdfSeedValue A signature field's seed values (/SV, ISO 32000-2, 12.7.5.5): constraints on how the field may be signed, honoured when signing (Phase 5 design Q7). PdfSeparationOptions How RenderSeparations(PdfRenderOptions?, PdfSeparationOptions?, CancellationToken) makes plates: the press profile behind the process inks, and which spot inks get plates of their own. PdfSeparations A page rendered as ink plates (Phase 8 design Q4, Q5): one gray raster per process and spot ink, drawn by a true multi-ink renderer, so overprint, knockout and blend modes act on the inks as a press prints them. It measures total area coverage (TAC), the sum of every plate in percent, and draws a heat map of it. Dispose it to free the plates. PdfSetOcgStateAction A set-OCG-state action (12.6.4.13): turns optional content groups (layers) on or off. PdfSignOptions How a document is signed (Phase 5 design, 5.1). PdfSignature A signature or document timestamp in a signed signature field (ISO 32000-2, 12.8): its value dictionary, the bytes it signs and the revision those bytes are. Reading checks nothing cryptographic; ByteRangeIssues reports what is wrong with the byte range itself. PdfSignatureAppearance Where and how a signature shows on a page (Phase 5 design Q6). Signatures are invisible unless given one: the Default(int, RectF, Raster?) layout shows the signer's name with the date, reason and location; Draw(int, RectF, Action<PdfCanvas>) lets the caller draw anything with the same PdfCanvas as pages. The appearance is part of the signed revision, so it is drawn before the file is hashed. PdfSignatureChange One change found in a revision after a signature, with how it is judged and why. PdfSignatureField A signature field (12.7.5.5). Signatures reads the signatures in signed fields (Phase 5). PdfSignatureReport What verifying a signature found (Phase 5 design Q8): separate verdicts for integrity, the certificate chain, the timestamp, revocation and the changes made since signing, with the reasons behind each. PdfSigner Who signs and with which key (Phase 5 design Q3): a certificate with its private key, or any RSA or ECDsa object with the certificate it belongs to. A subclass of RSA or ECDsa reaches a smart card, an HSM or a cloud key service, since Egap only ever asks it to sign the signed attributes. A signature made somewhere else entirely goes through PrepareSignatureAsync(string, PdfSignOptions, Stream, CancellationToken) instead. PdfSquareAnnotation A square annotation (12.5.6.8): a rectangle drawn inside the annotation's rectangle. PdfSquigglyAnnotation A squiggly underline annotation (12.5.6.10, PDF 1.4). PdfStamp A stamp: text, an image or another page drawn on every page (or the pages chosen) as removable page furniture (Phase 7 design 7.3, Q10 and Q11). Make one with Text(string), Watermark(string), Bates(PdfBatesSequence), Image(Raster, double, double) or Page(PdfPage), then set its placement with with. PdfStampAnnotation A rubber stamp annotation (12.5.6.12): a stamp such as Approved or Draft. PdfStampResult What Stamp(PdfStamp) did. PdfStream A PDF stream: a dictionary followed by data. A stream is always an indirect object. Its data stays in the file until it is asked for, and an unchanged stream is copied raw when the file is saved. PdfStrikeOutAnnotation A strikeout annotation (12.5.6.10). PdfString A PDF string: a sequence of bytes, written either as a literal (...) or as hex <...>. A string read from a file keeps its bytes and its form, so an unchanged string writes back the same way. PdfStructureElement An element of the structure tree (ISO 32000-1 14.7.2, Phase 5 design Q14): its type, the text properties assistive technology reads (title, language, alternate, actual and expanded text), attributes and classes, and its children. Changes are written to the element's dictionary at once; the parent tree is rebuilt when the document is saved. PdfStructureNode A child of a structure element (ISO 32000-1 14.7.2): another element, a marked-content sequence or an object. PdfStructureTree A document's logical structure (ISO 32000-1 14.7, Phase 5 design Q14): the tree of structure elements, the role map from the document's own types to standard ones, and the class map of shared attributes. Elements are read from and written to the file's objects directly; the parent tree that leads from page content back to elements is rebuilt from the elements when the document is saved after a change. Page import and merge bring the elements of the pages they copy. PdfSubmitFormAction A submit-form action (12.7.6.2): sends field values to a URL. PdfTextAnnotation A text annotation (12.5.6.4): a sticky note shown as an icon, its text in a popup. PdfTextChange One change in the text (Phase 7 design Q12). PdfTextField A text field (12.7.5.3): text the user types, on one line or several. PdfTextFieldOptions How a new text field works. PdfTextGlyph One glyph of a page's text (Phase 3 design Q10): the text it stands for, its box in the page's default user space, its font, size and fill colour. A span with /ActualText gives one glyph for the whole span, holding that text. PdfTextLine A line: words on one baseline, in one direction. PdfTextMarkupAnnotation A text markup annotation (12.5.6.10): highlight, underline, squiggly underline or strikeout over text, given as quadrilaterals. PdfTextMatch A run of text found on a page. PdfTextOptions How GetText(PdfTextOptions?) builds words and lines. PdfTextPage A page's text (Phase 3 design Q10): every glyph shown, built into words and lines. PdfTextWord A word: glyphs with no space and no wide gap between them. PdfTimestampClient An RFC 3161 timestamp authority, reached through the caller's HttpClient (Phase 5 design Q5): Egap never opens a connection on its own and has no default server. The client carries the caller's proxy, timeouts, retries and any credentials the authority wants. Requests are built and responses checked with .NET's Rfc3161TimestampRequest. PdfUnderlineAnnotation An underline annotation (12.5.6.10). PdfUriAction A URI action (12.6.4.8): opens a URI, usually a web address. PdfVerifyOptions Options for verifying a signature (Phase 5 design Q8): the trust anchors are the caller's, there is no built-in trust list, and nothing is fetched from the network unless a revocation source says so. PdfVisualChange Where two matching pages render differently. PdfWarning One repair made while reading a damaged file. In strict mode the same problem throws a PdfException. PdfWidgetAnnotation A widget annotation (12.5.6.19): how a form field appears on a page. PdfXConvertOptions Options for Convert(PdfDocument, PdfXConformance, PdfXConvertOptions?, CancellationToken). PdfXConverter Checks documents against PDF/X and converts them to it (Phase 8 design Q9, Q10). PDF/X-4 and X-6 are checked and converted; X-1a and X-3 too when the file has no transparency, which conversion does not flatten; X-4p, X-5g, X-5pg and X-6p are checked only; X-5n and X-6n are checked, with an n-colorant output intent. Conversion fixes in place what it can (output intent, trim and bleed boxes, identification and metadata, trapping key, fonts, colours through PdfColorConverter, transfer functions, annotations in the print area, actions) and reports every fix; when a rule cannot be met nothing is changed. Issues are PdfAIssues, as for PDF/A. No open validator judges PDF/X: Acrobat Preflight or PackzView is the full judge. PdfXfa The XFA form of a document (12.7.8, hub Q7): the form's /XFA, one XDP stream or an array of named packets. Egap keeps it on save as it is, reads its packets, and keeps the datasets packet in step with the AcroForm field values: setting a field's value writes it into the data too. A static XFA form converts to a plain AcroForm with ConvertToAcroForm(); a dynamic one, which has no AcroForm fields of its own to fall back on, is reported by IsDynamic and not converted. PosterOptions How Poster(PdfDocument, PosterOptions?) cuts pages into tiles. Structs Length A length on the page, held in points (1/72 inch) and made from points, millimetres, centimetres or inches, so sizes in different units cannot be mixed up. It converts to and from a double in points without a cast, so it can be passed wherever a size in points is asked for, and a plain number still works wherever a Length is. PdfByteRange One range of signed bytes: Length bytes from Start. PdfChoiceOption An option of a choice field: the value exported when it is selected, and the text shown. PdfGlyph One glyph shown by a text operator, as a PdfContentWalker reports it: the code shown, the font and the text rendering matrix (9.4.4) that maps the glyph from text space, scaled by the font size, to the space the walk started in. PdfMatrix A transformation matrix as PDF writes it (8.3.3): [a b c d e f], mapping a point (x, y) to (a·x + c·y + e, b·x + d·y + f). PdfPageSize A sheet size in points, such as A4. PdfPathSegment One segment of a path. For a curve, Control1 and Control2 are its control points. PdfPoint A point in default user space, as annotations give vertices, lines and quadrilaterals. PdfQuad A quadrilateral on the page, such as the area of a matched run of text on one line, in default user space. PdfRectangle A rectangle in PDF user space (7.9.5), as page boxes are given: the lower-left and upper-right corners, with y going up. PdfRgbColor A colour in DeviceRGB, each component from 0 to 1, as outline items and annotations give one. PdfStructureType A structure element type (ISO 32000-1 14.8.4, Phase 5 design Q14): one of the standard types, or a document's own type that its role map maps to a standard one. Any name converts to a type. PdfVerticalMetrics A vertical font's metrics for one glyph (9.7.4.3), in thousandths of text space, from /W2 or /DW2. Enums BookletBinding Which edge a booklet is bound on. NUpOrder The order pages fill the cells of an N-up sheet. PadesLevel The PAdES baseline level a signature is made at (ETSI EN 319 142-1; Phase 5 design Q4). PdfAConformance A PDF/A part and conformance level a file claims (ISO 19005; Phase 5 design Q11). PdfAnnotationFlags Annotation flags (12.5.3, table 167). PdfAnnotationRendering Which annotations a render draws (design Q12). PdfAntialiasing What a render anti-aliases (design Q11). PdfAppearanceKind Which appearance of an annotation (12.5.5). PdfAttachmentRelationship How an attached file relates to the document (/AFRelationship, ISO 32000-2 14.13.2). PdfBlackText How colour conversion treats black and gray text and thin rules. PdfBorderStyle A border style (12.5.4, table 168). PdfByteRangeIssues What is wrong with a signature's /ByteRange (Phase 5 design, 5.1); None when nothing is. PdfCanvasCoordinates Which coordinates a PdfCanvas draws in (Phase 3 design Q13). PdfCanvasPlacement Where new drawing goes on a page that already has content (Phase 3 design Q5). PdfCertificateSeedFlags Which certificate seed values a signer must follow (/Ff of a certificate seed value dictionary, ISO 32000-2, Table 238). PdfCertification The changes a certification signature allows after it (DocMDP /P, ISO 32000-2, 12.8.2.2); the values are the numbers in the file. PdfChangeVerdict How a change made after a signature is judged (Phase 5 design Q8). PdfColorSpaceKinds Kinds of colour space, as a print profile allows them and a preflight report lists them. PdfCompression Whether a rewrite packs objects into object streams and the cross-reference into a stream (design Q7). PdfDestinationFit How a destination fits its page in the window (12.3.2.2). PdfEncryptionKind The kinds of PdfEncryption. PdfFieldFlags Field flags (12.7.4.1, tables 227, 229, 231 and 233). Some bits mean different things for different field types. PdfFieldLockAction Which fields a field lock covers (/Action, ISO 32000-2, Table 236). PdfFlattenFilter Which annotations flattening draws, as qpdf's --flatten-annotations chooses them; hidden ones never. PdfFontFlags The flags of a font descriptor (9.8.2, table 121). PdfFontType The kind of a PDF font, its /Subtype (9.5). PdfHighlightMode How a link or widget looks while pressed (12.5.6.5, table 176). PdfInvoiceProfile The Factur-X and ZUGFeRD profile, how much of the invoice the XML holds. PdfInvoiceStandard The e-invoice standard an embedded invoice follows. PdfLineEnding A line ending style (12.5.6.7, table 179), named as in the file. PdfPageBox Which of a page's boxes (14.11.2) a render shows. PdfPageLabelStyle How the number in a page label is written (12.4.2). PdfPathPaint How a path is painted (8.5.3): any mix of stroking, filling and clipping, or none for n on its own. PdfPathVerb What a path segment does (8.5.2). PdfPermissions What the owner of an encrypted file allows (ISO 32000-2, Table 22). The flags are advisory: anyone who can open the file can read everything in it, so honouring them is the caller's job (design Q5). The values are the bits of /P. PdfPreflightItemKind What a PdfPreflightItem reports. PdfRedactImages What redaction does to an image the area covers (Phase 5 design Q9). PdfRedactPaths What redaction does to vector line art the area covers (Phase 5 design Q9). PdfRenderIntent What a render is for, which decides the annotations (by their flags) and layers (by their usage) that show. PdfReplyType How a markup annotation relates to the one it points at with /IRT (12.5.6.2). PdfSaveMode How a document is saved. PdfSeedValueFlags Which seed values a signer must follow (/Ff of a seed value dictionary, ISO 32000-2, Table 237); a value whose bit is clear is only a suggestion. PdfSignatureFormat How the signature value is encoded (/SubFilter, Phase 5 design Q4). PdfSignatureKind What a signature is (ISO 32000-2, 12.8). PdfSpotConversion What colour conversion does with spot colours (Separation and DeviceN). PdfStampSubtype The kind of page furniture a stamp is marked as (ISO 32000-2 14.8.2.2, pagination artifacts). PdfTextAlignment How text is aligned in a free text annotation or a field (/Q). PdfTextChangeKind How a run of words changed. PdfTextOrder The order GetText(PdfTextOptions?) puts text in (Phase 3 design Q10). PdfVerdict One verdict of a signature report (Phase 5 design Q8). PdfWarningCode What kind of repair a PdfWarning records. PdfXConformance A PDF/X version a file is checked against or converted to (ISO 15930; Phase 8 design Q9). StampAnchor Where on the shown page a stamp is anchored: one of nine points, the stamp's own box aligned to it.

articles/cli/commands.html.title: egap command reference | Egap
articles/cli/commands.html.summary: egap command reference Every command, its arguments and its options, as egap <command> --help shows them. This page is written from the command tree by the tests, so it always matches the tool. The guide explains the conventions all commands share. Options every command takes: --help, --verbose, --debug, --quiet, --limit, --strict. egap info egap info <inputs>... [options] Show what PDFs are: version, pages and sizes, encryption, signatures, PDF/A claim, forms and attachments; with --all, much more. articles/cli/index.html.title: The egap command | Egap
articles/cli/index.html.summary: The egap command egap turns HTML, Markdown, DOCX and images into PDF, and inspects, merges, splits, stamps, redacts, fills, signs and checks PDFs from a shell, a build script or an AI assistant. It is a .NET tool built on Egap's public API, so it does what the library does, with the same defaults. Every command is listed with its options in the command reference. dotnet tool install --global Egap.Cli egap info report.pdf egap convert notes.md -o notes.pdf --page-size A4 --footer "Page {page} of {total-pages}" egap merge cover.pdf body.pdf#2-z appendix.pdf -o book.pdf Conventions Every command follows the same rules, which are those of Egami's egami command. Inputs. Files, globs (*, ?, [abc], **) that egap expands itself, so they behave the same in every shell, folders with --recursive, or - for standard input. Several inputs run at once (--jobs); a file that fails is reported and the rest carry on, unless --fail-fast. Outputs. -o takes a file, a folder, a template such as out/{name}.pdf ({name}, {ext}, {dir}, {index}, {page}) or - for standard output. egap never writes over an input unless you give --in-place, and every output is written to a temporary file first, so a failed command leaves the old file as it was. Pages. One syntax everywhere: 1,3,5-10, z for the last page, r2 for the second to last, 10-1 backwards, :odd and :even, x to leave pages out (1-z,x5). A file in merge takes its pages after a #. Lengths and sizes. 12mm, 1.5cm, 1in or 72pt; page sizes A3, A4, A5, Letter, Legal, Tabloid or WxH such as 210mmx297mm. Passwords. --password-env NAME reads an environment variable and --password-file path the first line of a file; with neither, egap asks on the terminal. --password works too, with a warning, since it lands in shell history. Saving. An edit is appended as an incremental update, so signatures stay valid where the change allows; a new document (convert, merge, split, impose) is written whole. --rewrite, --linearize and --compress override that. An edit that would break a signature stops unless --allow-invalidating-signatures. Redaction, sanitizing and PDF/A and PDF/X conversion always write the whole file, so no earlier revision keeps what they removed. Output and exit codes. Text on standard output, warnings and errors on standard error (-q and -v set how much). Report commands take --json, with a versioned schema in docs/schemas. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 a file failed or a check found a problem (compare, verify, pdfa check, pdfx check, preflight), 2 a mistake in the command line, 3 a safety limit. Safety limits. --limit objects=2M,decoded=512MB,ratio=200,depth=64,xref=512 or EGAP_LIMITS; --strict refuses damaged files instead of repairing them. Network. None, except a timestamp authority and OCSP or CRL fetches while signing, and remote HTML resources with --allow-network. Inspecting egap info *.pdf egap info contract.pdf --all egap info "scans/**/*.pdf" --json egap text report.pdf --pages 1-3 egap text report.pdf --json -o words.json egap render report.pdf -o thumbs/ --format png --dpi 72 egap render slides.pdf -o slide.jpg --fit 1920x1080 --pages 1 egap metadata show report.pdf --xmp --outline egap form list application.pdf --json egap attach list invoice.pdf Converting convert picks the direction from the output's extension. HTML reads its images and style sheets from its own folder only, unless --allow-path or --allow-network says otherwise. egap convert page.html -o page.pdf --page-size Letter --margins 20mm --tagged egap convert "docs/*.md" -o out/{name}.pdf --toc pages --header "|{title}|" egap convert letter.docx -o letter.pdf --pdfa 2b egap convert photo.jpg -o photo.pdf egap convert report.pdf -o report.docx egap convert report.pdf -o report.md --mode flow egap convert draft.docx -o review.pdf --comments annotations # comments as PDF annotations egap convert report.docx -o report.pdf --embed-source # a hybrid PDF: converts back to the DOCX egap convert notes.md -o notes.html egap convert page.html -o page.pdf --allow-network Pages egap merge a.pdf b.pdf#2-z c.pdf#1,3 -o all.pdf egap split book.pdf -o chapters/ --range 1-12 --range 13-40 --range 41-z egap split scans.pdf -o "out/{name}-{page:000}.pdf" --every 2 egap pages scan.pdf --rotate 90:2-4 --delete 5 -o fixed.pdf egap pages book.pdf --select 1,3-z --blank end --label 1:r --label 3:D -o book2.pdf egap impose handout.pdf --nup 2x2 --sheet A4 -o handout-4up.pdf egap impose zine.pdf --booklet -o zine-booklet.pdf egap stamp report.pdf --page-numbers -o numbered.pdf egap stamp draft.pdf --watermark DRAFT --opacity 0.2 -o watermarked.pdf egap stamp "evidence/*.pdf" --bates ACME- --bates-digits 6 -o stamped/ Editing and protecting egap metadata set report.pdf --title "Annual report" --author "Ada Lovelace" --in-place egap metadata set report.pdf --outline outline.json -o report2.pdf egap metadata strip report.pdf -o clean.pdf egap optimize scan.pdf --preset ebook -o small.pdf egap encrypt report.pdf --owner-password-env OWNER --user-password-env READER --allow print -o locked.pdf egap decrypt locked.pdf --password-env OWNER -o open.pdf egap redact statement.pdf --regex "\d{4} \d{4} \d{4} \d{4}" -o redacted.pdf egap redact form.pdf --rect 1:20mm,250mm,80mm,10mm -o redacted.pdf egap sanitize upload.pdf --keep metadata -o safe.pdf egap form fill application.pdf --data answers.json --flatten -o filled.pdf egap attach add report.pdf --file data.csv --relationship data -o report-with-data.pdf egap attach extract report.pdf -o attachments/ egap invoice embed invoice.pdf --xml factur-x.xml -o e-invoice.pdf Signing and checking sign always appends its signature as an incremental update. The certificate comes from a PFX file, a PEM certificate and key, or the Windows and macOS certificate store. egap sign contract.pdf --cert me.pfx --cert-password-env PFX_PASSWORD --reason Approved -o signed.pdf egap sign contract.pdf --cert me.pem --key me-key.pem --level b-t --timestamp http://timestamp.example.com -o signed.pdf egap sign contract.pdf --cert-store 3F2A9C1E5B7D4E8A9C217D4E5F6A8B90C1D2E3F4 --visible 1:20mm,250mm,60mm,20mm -o signed.pdf egap verify signed.pdf --trust root.cer egap verify "contracts/*.pdf" --system-trust --json egap compare v1.pdf v2.pdf --markup changes.pdf egap pdfa check archive.pdf egap pdfa convert report.pdf --level 2b -o report-a.pdf egap pdfa check report.pdf --ua Print production egap preflight flyer.pdf --profile sheetfed-coated egap preflight flyer.pdf --max-ink 300 --bleed 3mm --json egap pdfx convert flyer.pdf --level x-4 --output-condition FOGRA39 -o flyer-x4.pdf egap pdfx check flyer-x4.pdf --level x-4 egap separations flyer.pdf -o plates --coverage --json egap color flyer.pdf --target FOGRA39 -o flyer-cmyk.pdf Scans and mail merge ocr makes scans searchable through an OCR program you install, such as Tesseract: it runs the program on each page image and adds the words as invisible text. The output is PDF/A-2b unless --pdfa none. Pages that already have text are left alone; --mode redo replaces an earlier OCR layer and --mode force reads every page. egap ocr scan.pdf --engine-command "tesseract {image} {output} -l {langs} --dpi {dpi} hocr" --lang eng -o searchable.pdf egap ocr "scans/*.pdf" --engine-command "tesseract {image} {output} -l {langs} hocr" --lang eng+nor --mode redo -o "ocr/{name}.pdf" egap ocr-layer scan.pdf --hocr "ocr/page-{page}.hocr" -o searchable.pdf egap clean scan.pdf --deskew --remove-blank-pages --grayscale -o tidy.pdf egap merge-data letter.docx --data people.json -o letters.pdf egap merge-data letter.docx --data people.csv --each --name-field Name -o "letters/{name}.pdf" Pipelines and workflows run chains steps over each input, joined by a bare +. Every edit command is a step with the same options, append adds the pages of other files, and save writes; there may be several saves, and the last step must be one. egap run --list lists the steps. egap run scan.pdf pages --rotate 90:1 + clean --deskew + stamp --page-numbers + save out.pdf --linearize egap run "in/*.pdf" --jobs 8 stamp --watermark CONFIDENTIAL + save "out/{name}.pdf" + encrypt --owner-password-env OWNER + save "locked/{name}.pdf" egap run cover.pdf append body.pdf#2-z + metadata --title Book + save book.pdf egap run report.pdf --dry-run pages --delete 2 + save "out/{name}.pdf" egap run --save-workflow print.json --dry-run pdfx --level x-4 --output-condition FOGRA39 + save "print/{name}.pdf" egap run "jobs/*.pdf" --workflow print.json A workflow file holds the same steps as JSON, each step's options named without their dashes: { "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inexin/Egap/main/docs/schemas/egap-workflow-1.json", "egap": 1, "steps": [ { "op": "pages", "rotate": [ "90:1" ] }, { "op": "stamp", "page-numbers": true }, { "op": "save", "path": "out/{name}.pdf", "linearize": true } ] } AI assistants egap mcp serves every command as a tool over the Model Context Protocol, for Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and other assistants. Tools read and write only inside the folders the assistant opened and those given with --allow; sign, encrypt and decrypt are offered only with --allow-sign, and passwords come only from environment variables. ocr is never offered, since it runs the program the call names. egap mcp --allow ~/Documents/pdfs egap mcp --allow ./contracts --allow-sign To add it to an assistant, register the command egap with the argument mcp, or, without installing the tool, dnx with Egap.Cli --yes -- mcp. More tools egap <name> runs a program called egap-<name> from the PATH, as git and dotnet do. egap preview therefore starts egap-preview when the Egap.Preview tool is installed: egap preview letter.docx JSON schemas Command Schema info --json egap-info-1.json text --json egap-text-1.json metadata show --json egap-metadata-1.json form list --json egap-form-1.json compare --json egap-compare-1.json verify --json egap-verify-1.json pdfa check --json, pdfx check --json egap-pdfa-1.json preflight --json egap-preflight-1.json separations --json egap-separations-1.json run --workflow egap-workflow-1.json

articles/formats/docling-json.html.title: Docling JSON | Egap
articles/formats/docling-json.html.summary: Docling JSON Docling JSON is the DoclingDocument format that Docling writes: texts, tables, pictures and list groups, linked into reading order, each with its role and its box on the page. Egap.Documents writes a PDF's analysed page layouts as Docling JSON and reads Docling JSON back, from Docling or from Egap, without an add-on package. The schema version written, and the newest read, is DoclingJson.SchemaVersion. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("report.pdf"); IReadOnlyList<PdfPageLayout> pages = PdfLayoutAnalyzer.Analyze(pdf); DoclingJson.Write(pages, "report.json", new DoclingJsonOptions { Name = "report", Indented = true }); IReadOnlyList<PdfPageLayout> back = DoclingJson.Read(File.ReadAllText("report.json")); // page layouts again Document flow = Document.Load("report.json"); // or a flow document Writing DoclingJson.Write takes the page layouts that PdfLayoutAnalyzer finds (see PDF to documents). Roles become Docling's labels, boxes become provenance with the page number and a box from the page's bottom left, as PDF measures, and page headers and footers go to the furniture layer. Egap's own role and confidence go in each item's meta. Option Default Does Name "document" The document's name, Docling's name FileName, Source None The source file's name and bytes; with Source set, the origin is written with its hash Indented false Indents the JSON for reading Images DataUris How pictures carry their image: DataUris (the file stands alone), Files or Omit ImagesFolder <name>.images The folder beside the JSON that Files writes images to, each image once, named in reading order ImageResolver None Stores each picture's image and returns the URI to write FigureResolution 200 Pixels per inch at which figures drawn on the page become images, 10 to 1200 MinImageSize 6 Figures smaller than this on both sides, in points, get no image (bullets, rules, specks) Reading DoclingJson.Read gives page layouts: texts become blocks with their roles, tables keep their cells, pictures become figures, all in reading order. The JSON keeps no line breaks or fonts, so each text becomes one line with its words spread over its box. DoclingJson.ToDocument, and Document.Load for a file that names the DoclingDocument schema, give a flow document instead: texts as paragraphs in the styles of their roles, list items in lists, tables with their cells and spans, pictures with the images the JSON carries, and page headers and footers in each section's header and footer. Docling JSON holds page layouts, not flow documents, so Document.Save does not write it; use DoclingJson.Write.

articles/formats/docx.html.title: DOCX | Egap
articles/formats/docx.html.summary: DOCX Egap.Documents reads and writes Word's files: documents (.docx), templates (.dotx) and their macro-enabled forms (.docm, .dotm), strict and transitional. It needs no add-on package. Reading A Word file reads into the model with Word's style model, lists numbered as Word numbers them, tables, fields, comments and tracked changes; the flow documents guide shows what you can do with them. What the model does not name travels along in each node's extension data. Macros are kept and never run. An old binary Word file (.doc) is recognized and refused with an error that says so. DocxLoadOptions.Limits keeps untrusted files in bounds (see Limits). using Egap.Documents; Document report = Document.LoadDocx("report.docx", out IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning> warnings); DocxKind? kind = DocxFormat.KindOf(report); // Document, Template or a macro-enabled kind report.SaveAsDocx("report-copy.docx"); // what the model does not name is kept DocxFormat.Save(report, "report.dotx", new DocxSaveOptions { Kind = DocxKind.Template }); Word compatibility Word lays a file out by the rules of the Word version that made it: DocumentSettings.CompatibilityMode says which (15 for Word 2013 and later, 14 for 2010, 12 for 2007, 11 and below for older files), and the settings part's compatibility options switch single layout rules on or off. Egap reads both and lays the document out by the same rules. DocumentSettings.WordCompatibility names each option Egap acts on. A flag is what the file or your code set, else the default for the compatibility mode, so changing the mode changes every flag nobody set: Flag When on AllowSpaceOfSameStyleInTable Contextual spacing is ignored in table cells. DoNotUseIndentAsNumberingTabStop The tab after a list label skips the hanging indent and goes to the next tab stop. SplitPageBreakAndParagraphMark After a page break that ends a paragraph, the paragraph mark takes a line on the next page. OverrideTableStyleFontSizeAndJustification A table style's font size and alignment win over an 11 or 12 point, left-aligned default paragraph style. EnableOpenTypeFeatures Runs' ligatures, contextual alternates, stylistic sets and number forms are used. DoNotBreakWrappedTables A floating table stays on one page. AllowTextAfterFloatingTableBreak Text may follow a floating table on the page where it breaks. TableIndentFromCellText A table's indent is measured to its first cell's text (Word before 2013; not saved to DOCX). A new document has Word 2013's options, and saving it writes them. A file's options go back as they were read; a flag you set is written, and the options Egap does not act on stay in the file and are listed in OtherSettings. using Egap.Documents; Document old = Document.LoadDocx("word-2007.docx"); WordCompatibility compat = old.Settings.WordCompatibility; bool legacyTables = !compat.OverrideTableStyleFontSizeAndJustification; string? ulTrailSpace = compat.OtherSettings.GetValueOrDefault("ulTrailSpace"); // "1" when the file has it compat.EnableOpenTypeFeatures = true; // shape with the runs' ligatures and number forms old.Settings.CompatibilityMode = 15; // the flags nobody set follow Word 2013's rules compat.UseModeDefaults(); // forget the file's values too Writing DOCX to DOCX is lossless: parts and paragraphs you did not edit are written as they were read. Saving to a path takes the kind from the extension, so report.dotx is a template; saving to a stream keeps the kind the document was read as (a new document is a .docx). DocxSaveOptions.Kind overrides both. A kind that holds no macros drops the macros a .docm or .dotm had. A document read from another format saves as DOCX with what Word can hold. Some things the model has Word does not: Word has no word spacing or overline; it keeps the OpenType features it knows (ligatures, number forms and spacing, stylistic sets, contextual alternates). See Text options. Paging settings on groups of blocks, clamped lines and balanced columns are not saved; the content is. See Page layout. Margin boxes at the top and bottom of the page are saved as a three-part table in the header or footer; those in the corners and at the sides are left out with a warning. Flex and grid containers are saved as borderless tables with their items in the cells, and a group with a box as a one-cell table; the cells keep the items' backgrounds, borders and padding, not rounded corners or shadows. See Flex and grid layout. An SVG picture is saved with the PNG stand-in in Picture.Fallback, as Word stores SVG pictures, so older readers show it too. Barcodes get one at 300 pixels per inch.

articles/formats/epub.html.title: EPUB | Egap
articles/formats/epub.html.summary: EPUB EPUB books come from the add-on package Egap.Documents.Html, the same one that reads and writes HTML. It reads EPUB 2 and EPUB 3 books into the document model and writes the model as an EPUB 3.3 book, so a DOCX, HTML or Markdown file can become an e-book and a book can become a PDF or a Word file. dotnet add package Egap.Documents.Html The format's class is EpubFormat, in namespace Egap.Documents. HtmlFormat.Register() at startup lets Document.Load, Document.Save and PdfConvert.FromFile handle .epub files too. Calling EpubFormat or the members it adds to Document (Document.LoadEpub, ToEpub, SaveAsEpub) needs no registration. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; Document book = Document.LoadEpub("novel.epub"); book.SaveAsPdf("novel.pdf"); Document.LoadDocx("handbook.docx").SaveAsEpub("handbook.epub"); Reading A book is read into one document. Each file of the book's reading order (its spine) becomes a section that starts on a new page, read through the HTML reader with the book's own style sheets, for screen media unless Media says "print". The cover image gets a section of its own at the start unless the first chapter already shows it. Links from one chapter to another become links inside the document, and an id that two chapters both use is renamed in the second. The book's table of contents (the EPUB 3 navigation document, or the EPUB 2 NCX) becomes the outline: each entry's target paragraph gets the entry's outline level unless it is a heading already, so a PDF made from the book gets the same bookmarks and a table of contents field lists the same entries. The package metadata becomes document properties: EPUB Document dc:title Properties.Title dc:creator (each) Properties.Author, joined with "; " dc:subject (each) Properties.Keywords, joined with "; " dc:description Properties.Comments dc:date Properties.Created dcterms:modified Properties.Saved dc:language The default language of the text dc:publisher, dc:rights, dc:contributor, the unique identifier Custom properties Publisher, Rights, Contributors, Identifier Fonts that the book's style sheets declare with @font-face are loaded into Document.EmbeddedFonts, with the IDPF and Adobe font obfuscation undone. Fixed-layout books (comics, picture books) are read with one section per page, the page the size of the page's viewport and its positioned content placed as the HTML reader places it. Audio, video, media overlays and scripts are left out with a MediaDropped warning; scripts never run. using Egap.Documents; Document book = EpubFormat.Load("novel.epub", out IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning> warnings, new EpubLoadOptions { Media = "print", UserStyleSheets = ["body { font-size: 11pt; }"], }); Option Default Does ResourceResolver None Fetches what a chapter links to outside the book by absolute URL, or returns null to leave it out Media "screen" The media the book's style sheets apply for: "screen" or "print" UserStyleSheets None Style sheets applied as the user's, after the default one and before the book's own Limits DocumentLimits defaults Entries, entry and total sizes, compression ratio and nesting (see Limits) Egap does not remove DRM. A book whose files are encrypted with Adobe ADEPT, Readium LCP, Apple FairPlay or any scheme other than font obfuscation throws a DocumentException that names the scheme. A book whose entries point outside the container is refused the same way, and nothing outside the book is fetched unless you give a resolver. Writing The document is written as an EPUB 3.3 book that EPUBCheck, the W3C validator, passes without errors: XHTML chapter files from the HTML writer, split where SplitAt says: at section breaks and at level 1 headings by default. A book read from EPUB keeps its own chapter files and their ids. A navigation document with the outline down to NavigationDepth levels, and for EPUB 2 reading systems a toc.ncx and a guide. The pictures, written once each; pictures in formats EPUB does not hold are written as PNG. The metadata from the document properties, with the book's identifier kept when it was read from EPUB, else a urn:uuid made from the title and author. Accessibility metadata from what the document has (schema:accessMode, accessibilityFeature, accessibilityHazard and a summary), as the EPUB Accessibility 1.1 specification asks, with the language and the pictures' alternative text. using Egap.Documents; Document report = Document.LoadDocx("report.docx"); EpubFormat.Save(report, "report.epub", new EpubSaveOptions { SplitAt = EpubSplit.HeadingLevel1, NavigationDepth = 2, CoverImage = new ImageData(File.ReadAllBytes("cover.jpg"), "image/jpeg"), EmbedFonts = true, }); Option Default Does SplitAt SectionBreak and HeadingLevel1 Where a new chapter file starts; None writes one file NavigationDepth 3 How many outline levels the table of contents shows (1 to 9) EmbedFonts Off Whether Document.EmbeddedFonts go into the book, subset to the characters used and obfuscated as EPUB says CoverImage None A picture for a cover page before the first chapter Identifier Kept, or made from the title and author The book's unique identifier AccessibilitySummary A sentence about what the book has The accessibility summary in the package Modified The document's saved time, else now The book's last-modified time Embedding fonts is a licence question only you can answer, so it is off until you turn it on. A reading system that lacks a font falls back to its own.

articles/formats/html.html.title: HTML | Egap
articles/formats/html.html.summary:
HTML HTML and XHTML come from the add-on package Egap.Documents.Html. It reads a page into the document model, styled through the CSS cascade, and writes the model back as HTML. It also brings HTML to PDF, HTML stamps and HTML page bands, and the two formats built on HTML: MHTML web archives and EPUB books. dotnet add package Egap.Documents.Html The format's class is HtmlFormat, in namespace Egap.Documents. Call HtmlFormat.Register() once at startup so that Document.Load, Document.Save and PdfConvert.FromFile handle .html files too, and .mht, .mhtml and .epub. Calling HtmlFormat or the members it adds to Document (Document.ParseHtml, Document.LoadHtml, ToHtml, SaveAsHtml) needs no registration. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; HtmlFormat.Register(); // once at startup: Document.Load and Save know .html Document page = Document.LoadHtml("invoice.html"); page.SaveAsDocx("invoice.docx"); string html = Document.LoadDocx("report.docx").ToHtml(); PdfConvert.FromHtml("

Invoice

Total: 120 EUR

", "invoice.pdf"); Reading HTML is parsed by AngleSharp as browsers parse it, and styled through Egami.Css's cascade with HTML's default style sheet, for print media unless Media says "screen". The computed styles become paragraphs, runs, lists, tables, and flex and grid containers (CSS layout). Scripts never run, and nothing outside the page is fetched unless you pass a resolver: using Egap.Documents; Document page = HtmlFormat.Load("invoice.html", new HtmlLoadOptions { BaseUri = new Uri("https://example.com/"), ResourceResolver = uri => File.Exists(uri.LocalPath) ? File.ReadAllBytes(uri.LocalPath) : null, }); Option Default Does BaseUri None The address relative URLs (images, style sheets) are resolved against ResourceResolver None Fetches what the page links to by absolute URL, or returns null to leave it out; data: URLs need none Encoding UTF-8 when the bytes are valid UTF-8, else windows-1252 The encoding of bytes when neither a byte order mark nor a meta charset names one Media "print" The media the style sheets apply for: "print" or "screen" UserStyleSheets None Style sheets applied as the user's, after the default one and before the page's own Kashida KashidaLevel.None How far text-align: justify paragraphs stretch Arabic lines with tatweels; CSS has no kashida value and browsers justify at spaces, so none by default Limits DocumentLimits defaults The largest page and how deep elements are read as structure (see Limits) PdfConvert.FromFile reads an HTML file's images and style sheets from the file's own folder, or from PdfConvertOptions.BaseDirectory when set, and never from the network. What CSS and HTML map to Besides fonts, colours, spacing, borders, lists and tables, these read into the model: Form controls (text inputs, check boxes, radio buttons, selects and text areas) are read as content controls that hold their values, as Word's are, so they keep their place in the text and a PDF export can turn them into form fields. word-spacing, text-decoration: overline, font-feature-settings, font-variant-ligatures, font-variant-numeric, word-break and overflow-wrap set the text options. break-inside: avoid on a box of several blocks makes a group that is kept on one page, and -webkit-line-clamp clamps a paragraph to a number of lines (see Page layout). @page margin box rules such as @top-left and @bottom-center, with counter(page) and counter(pages), become margin boxes. An element with position: running(name) leaves the body and shows in the boxes whose content is element(name). Margin boxes are written back as the same rules.
is read as a table of contents field. CSS layout display: flex and display: grid read into flex and grid containers, laid out as browsers lay them out and broken across pages between lines and rows. Each child element is an item, and text directly in the container an item of its own. CSS Read Flex containers flex-direction, flex-wrap, flex-flow, justify-content, align-items, align-content, gap, row-gap, column-gap Flex items flex, flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, order, align-self Grid containers grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows (lengths, %, fr, auto, min-content, max-content, minmax(), fit-content(), repeat() with a count, auto-fill or auto-fit), grid-template-areas, grid-template, grid-auto-rows, grid-auto-columns, grid-auto-flow with dense, the gaps, justify-items, align-items, justify-content and place-items Grid items grid-area (a name or lines), grid-row, grid-column and their -start and -end forms, span, negative lines, justify-self, align-self, place-self Boxes margin, padding, border, background-color, border-radius, box-shadow (the first outer shadow), width, height, min-height and box-sizing on containers and items Positioned boxes position: absolute and fixed with top, right, bottom, left, width, height and z-index Pages break between a container's lines and rows, and inside a line or row too tall for the room left, between its items' lines of text and table rows, as browsers break them. A block with border-radius or box-shadow becomes a group with a box around its blocks; other blocks keep their borders and background as paragraph borders and shading. A table with float: left or float: right floats at that side of the column with the text wrapping beside it, and is written back with the float. An absolutely positioned box becomes a text box floating in front of the text (behind it for a negative z-index), placed on the first page's body area, or from its positioned parent's first line; a fixed box goes in the header, so it shows on every page. position: sticky, subgrid, masonry, named grid lines and inline-flex and inline-grid boxes are not laid out as such; the last two read as inline content. Writing The model is written as HTML in UTF-8, with what HTML cannot hold returned as warnings. Option Default Does ImageWriter None Stores a picture and returns the URL the page uses for it, such as a file beside the page EmbedImages true Embeds pictures no writer stored as data: URLs WritePageSetup true Writes the page size, margins and simple headers and footers as @page rules HTML to PDF PdfConvert.FromHtml turns HTML into a PDF in one call, with page size, margins, header and footer bands and a table of contents. PdfStamp.Html lays out a piece of HTML as a stamp on every page of a PDF, and PageBand.Html makes a header or footer band styled with the page's own style sheets. PDF export and conversion shows each one.

articles/formats/index.html.title: Document formats | Egap
articles/formats/index.html.summary: Document formats Egap.Documents reads each format below into one document model and writes the model back out, so any format it reads can be saved as any format it writes. DOCX, PDF, plain text and Docling JSON are built in. HTML, MHTML and EPUB come from the add-on package Egap.Documents.Html, and Markdown from Egap.Documents.Markdown. Each format has its own page with its options and what it keeps. This page covers what they share: loading and saving without naming the format, how a file's format is found, warnings and limits. At a glance Format Package Reads Writes DOCX Egap.Documents DOCX, DOTX, DOCM and DOTM, strict and transitional The same four kinds; DOCX to DOCX keeps what the model does not name EPUB Egap.Documents.Html EPUB 2 and 3 books, a section per chapter, the table of contents as the outline; books under DRM refused EPUB 3.3 with a navigation document, a toc.ncx and accessibility metadata HTML Egap.Documents.Html HTML and XHTML, parsed as browsers parse it and styled through the CSS cascade HTML (UTF-8), with the page setup as @page rules Markdown Egap.Documents.Markdown CommonMark with GitHub's extensions and YAML front matter GitHub Flavored Markdown (UTF-8) MHTML Egap.Documents.Html Web archives as Chromium, Edge and Word save them One-file web archives in Chromium's shape Plain text Egap.Documents One paragraph per line The text in reading order, for search and indexing Docling JSON Egap.Documents DoclingDocument JSON, from Docling or from Egap Page layouts of a PDF, through DoclingJson.Write PDF Egap.Documents Pages analysed into blocks, headings, lists, tables and figures Tagged PDF and PDF/A PDF in and out is covered in PDF export and conversion. Loading and saving Document.Load and Document.Save work out the format by themselves. Load looks at the file's first bytes and, for text, at its extension; Save goes by the extension. DOCX, PDF, plain text and Docling JSON need nothing more. HTML, MHTML, EPUB and Markdown join them once you register their add-on at startup; until then, loading such a file throws a NotSupportedException that names the package and the call to make. Document.Identify tells which format a file is in without loading it and without any add-on, so a program can say what a file needs. using Egap.Documents; HtmlFormat.Register(); // once at startup: Load and Save now read and write HTML MarkdownFormat.Register(); DocumentFormatKind kind = Document.Identify("upload.bin"); // Pdf, Docx, Epub, Html, Mhtml, Markdown, Text, DoclingJson or Unknown Document notes = TextFormat.Load("notes.txt"); // one paragraph per line Identify decides in this order: A ZIP package whose first entry is EPUB's mimetype is Epub. Another ZIP package, or an old binary Word file, is Docx. Reading an old binary Word file fails with an error that says so. %PDF- in the first 1024 bytes is Pdf. Text whose extension names HTML (.html, .htm, .xhtml), MHTML (.mht, .mhtml), Markdown (.md, .markdown, .mdown, .mkd) or plain text (.txt, .text) is that format. Text that starts with MIME header lines naming multipart/related is Mhtml. A JSON object that names the DoclingDocument schema is DoclingJson. Text that starts with a tag is Html, and other text is Markdown. Binary data no format knows is Unknown. Save writes .docx, .dotx, .docm and .dotm as Word's, .pdf as PDF, .txt as plain text, and, once their add-on is registered, .html and .htm as HTML, .mht and .mhtml as MHTML, .epub as EPUB and .md and .markdown as Markdown. Any other extension throws an ArgumentException. Each format also has its own class (DocxFormat, HtmlFormat, EpubFormat, MarkdownFormat, TextFormat, DoclingJson) with its own options, and members on Document that forward to it, such as Document.LoadDocx, ToHtml and SaveAsMarkdown. Calling a format directly needs no Register(). Warnings Each Load has a form with an out list of ConversionWarnings for what could not be read as it was, and each Save returns a list of what the format could not hold, so a program can log it or show it. Limits DOCX, HTML, MHTML and EPUB files are read under DocumentLimits, so an untrusted file cannot exhaust memory. Pass your own in the format's load options (DocxLoadOptions.Limits, HtmlLoadOptions.Limits, EpubLoadOptions.Limits); a file past a limit throws a DocumentLimitException. Limit Default Does MaxEntries 10,000 The most entries a DOCX package or an EPUB book may have, or parts an MHTML archive MaxPartSize 512 MiB The largest uncompressed part, or the largest HTML page MaxTotalSize 2 GiB The most uncompressed bytes in all parts together MaxCompressionRatio 1,000 The highest compression ratio a part over 1 MiB may have, against ZIP bombs MaxDepth 256 How deep elements, tables and other structures may nest; deeper HTML is kept as plain text

articles/formats/markdown.html.title: Markdown | Egap
articles/formats/markdown.html.summary: Markdown Markdown comes from the add-on package Egap.Documents.Markdown. It reads CommonMark 0.31 with GitHub's extensions and YAML front matter into the document model, and writes the model as GitHub Flavored Markdown. Parsing is Markdig's. dotnet add package Egap.Documents.Markdown The format's class is MarkdownFormat, in namespace Egap.Documents. Call MarkdownFormat.Register() once at startup so that Document.Load, Document.Save and PdfConvert.FromFile handle .md files too. Calling MarkdownFormat or the members it adds to Document (Document.ParseMarkdown, Document.LoadMarkdown, ToMarkdown, SaveAsMarkdown) needs no registration. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; MarkdownFormat.Register(); // once at startup: Document.Load and Save know .md Document notes = Document.LoadMarkdown("notes.md"); notes.SaveAsDocx("notes.docx"); string markdown = Document.LoadDocx("report.docx").ToMarkdown(); PdfConvert.FromMarkdown("# Hello", "hello.pdf"); Reading Headings take the Heading 1 to 6 styles, code the HTML Code and HTML Preformatted styles, and lists Word list definitions built from their nesting. Files are read as UTF-8, or in the encoding a byte order mark names. MarkdownLoadOptions.Extensions picks what is read beyond CommonMark; all of GitHub's are on by default. Extension Reads Tables GitHub's pipe tables TaskLists Task list items, - [ ] and - [x] Strikethrough ~text~ and ~~text~~ Autolinks www., http://, https:// and e-mail addresses without angle brackets Footnotes [^label] with [^label]: definitions FrontMatter YAML front matter between --- lines at the very start, kept and mapped to document properties GitHub All of the above (the default); None reads CommonMark only using Egap.Documents; Document readme = MarkdownFormat.Load("README.md", new MarkdownLoadOptions { Extensions = MarkdownExtensions.GitHub }); Images are not fetched unless you pass MarkdownLoadOptions.ImageResolver, which gives the bytes for a URL or null. An image left unfetched becomes a picture that links to its URL. PdfConvert.FromFile reads a Markdown file's images from the file's own folder, and never from the network. Writing The model is written as GitHub Flavored Markdown in UTF-8 with LF line ends. Markdown holds less than the model, so each thing left out comes back as a warning. Front matter that was read is always written back. Pictures with an address of their own are written as links to it. The others, such as images embedded in a DOCX, follow Images: by default each one goes to ImageResolver, or, when saving to a file, into a folder beside it. Option Default Does Images Files What happens to pictures without an address: Files, DataUris (which GitHub and many viewers do not show), Placeholders (an HTML comment marks each one) or Omit (left out, with a warning) ImageResolver None Stores each image (browser-ready bytes, media type and a suggested name) and returns the address to write ImagesFolder <name>.images The folder beside the Markdown file that images are written to ImageWriter None Stores a picture and returns its address, or null to leave it out with a warning EmbedImages false The same as Images set to DataUris FigureResolution 150 Dots per inch for vector figures (Word's EMF and WMF pictures) written as PNG VectorFiguresAsSvg false Writes vector figures as SVG instead of PNG MinImageSize 6 Pictures narrower or shorter than this, in points, are left out as decoration (0 keeps them all) KeepBackgroundImages false Keeps pictures behind the text, such as page backgrounds and watermarks CaptionsAsFigures false Writes a picture with its caption as an HTML figure instead of an image and an italic paragraph WriteFrontMatter false Writes YAML front matter with the title and author when the document has them using Egap.Documents; Document report = Document.Load("report.docx"); report.SaveAsMarkdown("report.md", new MarkdownSaveOptions { WriteFrontMatter = true, VectorFiguresAsSvg = true }); Markdown to PDF PdfConvert.FromMarkdown turns Markdown into a PDF in one call. With PdfConvertOptions.TableOfContents set, a [TOC] paragraph marks where the table of contents goes. PDF export and conversion shows the options.

articles/formats/mhtml.html.title: MHTML | Egap
articles/formats/mhtml.html.summary: MHTML MHTML web archives (.mht, .mhtml) come from the add-on package Egap.Documents.Html. An archive holds an HTML page with its pictures, style sheets and fonts in one file, as Chromium, Edge and Word save pages.
