The page is read through the HTML reader, so everything HTML reads applies. dotnet add package Egap.Documents.Html The methods are on HtmlFormat, in namespace Egap.Documents: LoadMhtml and SaveMhtml, and ToMhtml and SaveAsMhtml on Document. HtmlFormat.Register() at startup lets Document.Load and Document.Save handle .mht and .mhtml files too. using Egap.Documents; Document page = HtmlFormat.LoadMhtml("saved-page.mhtml"); page.SaveAsDocx("saved-page.docx"); Document.LoadDocx("report.docx").SaveAsMhtml("report.mhtml"); Reading Archives in Chromium's shape and in Word's are both read. The page is the part the archive's start parameter names, or else its first HTML part, decoded in the charset the part names. Its links find the archive's other parts by their Content-Location or by cid: URL, base64 and quoted-printable bodies alike. What the archive does not hold is fetched only through HtmlLoadOptions.ResourceResolver, and never when you give none: using Egap.Documents; Document page = HtmlFormat.LoadMhtml("saved-page.mhtml", out IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning> warnings, new HtmlLoadOptions { Media = "screen", }); HtmlLoadOptions work as for HTML. Limits also bounds the archive: its parts (MaxEntries), the largest decoded part (MaxPartSize), all parts together (MaxTotalSize) and how deep multipart parts nest (MaxDepth). Writing The document is written in the shape Chromium saves pages in, which Chromium, Edge and Word open: a multipart/related message whose first part is the page in quoted-printable UTF-8, followed by each picture once and each of Document.EmbeddedFonts in base64, each with the Content-Location the page links to. HtmlSaveOptions work as for HTML; a picture that ImageWriter gives an address for is linked there instead of stored.

articles/formats/text.html.title: Plain text | Egap
articles/formats/text.html.summary: Plain text Egap.Documents reads and writes plain text without an add-on package. Reading turns each line into a paragraph; writing gives the document's text in reading order, for search and indexing. using Egap.Documents; Document notes = Document.LoadText("notes.txt"); // one paragraph per line Document report = Document.Load("report.docx"); string text = report.ToText(new TextSaveOptions { IncludeHeadersAndFooters = true }); report.SaveAsText("report.txt"); Reading Each line becomes a paragraph, a tab a tab and a form feed a page break. Lines may end in CR LF, LF or CR. A file is read as UTF-8 unless a byte order mark names UTF-16 or UTF-32. Document.Load reads .txt and .text files as plain text. Writing The text is written in reading order, one line per paragraph: list labels before their text with a tab, table rows as tab-separated cells, text boxes after the paragraph they are anchored in, and equations as their text. Field codes, deleted and hidden text, comments and pictures are left out. Files are written as UTF-8 without a byte order mark. Option Default Does IncludeHeadersAndFooters false Writes each section's headers before its body and its footers after it, each distinct text once IncludeNotes true Writes footnotes and endnotes at the end, each after its mark in brackets, with the mark in the text NewLine "\n" The line end written between paragraphs and table rows

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | Egap
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started Egap needs .NET 10. Add the package for what you need: dotnet add package Egap.Pdf # PDF files dotnet add package Egap.Documents # DOCX and plain text, documents to PDF, and PDF back to documents dotnet add package Egap.Documents.Html # HTML dotnet add package Egap.Documents.Markdown # Markdown Egami, the imaging library Egap draws with, comes along as a dependency. See Packages for what each one holds. Open, edit and save a PDF using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("in.pdf"); Console.WriteLine(pdf.Pages[0].ExtractText()); // lines in reading order pdf.Metadata.Title = "Quarterly report"; pdf.Outline.Add("Summary", PdfDestination.ToPage(pdf.Pages[0])); pdf.Save("out.pdf"); // incremental: the original bytes plus the changes Damaged files open too. Each repair Egap makes while reading is listed in pdf.Warnings; set PdfReadOptions.Strict to get an exception instead. Render a page using Egami; using Egami.Pixels; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("in.pdf"); using Raster<Rgba8> image = pdf.Pages[0].Render(new PdfRenderOptions { Dpi = 150 }); image.Save("page.png"); Turn a Word file into PDF using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; Document report = Document.Load("report.docx"); report.SaveAsPdf("report.pdf", new PdfExportOptions { Tagged = true }); Next The guides cover each area in more depth, grouped by package, and each document format has a page in Document formats. Every public type and member is in the API reference.

articles/guides/editing.html.title: Editing PDF files | Egap
articles/guides/editing.html.summary: Editing PDF files PdfDocument opens a file, lets you change its pages, navigation, annotations and forms, and saves it. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("in.pdf", new PdfReadOptions { Password = "secret" }); foreach (PdfWarning warning in pdf.Warnings) Console.WriteLine(warning); pdf.Pages.Move(0, pdf.Pages.Count - 1); // pages: insert, remove, move, labels pdf.Metadata.Title = "Quarterly report"; // Info and XMP kept in step pdf.Outline.Add("Summary", PdfDestination.ToPage(pdf.Pages[0])); pdf.Pages[0].Annotations.Add(new PdfHighlightAnnotation(PdfTextMarkupAnnotation.Quad(new PdfRectangle(72, 700, 300, 714)))); if (pdf.Form.TryGetField("customer.name", out PdfField field) && field is PdfTextField name) { name.Value = "Ada Lovelace"; // the widget is redrawn } pdf.Form.Flatten(); // fields drawn into the pages and removed pdf.Save("out.pdf"); // incremental: the original bytes plus the changes New form fields PdfForm adds text fields, check boxes, radio groups, combo and list boxes, push buttons and empty signature fields, each with a widget and an appearance drawn for it. A name with dots, such as customer.name, puts the field under a parent. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("blank.pdf"); pdf.Form.AddTextField("customer.name", 0, new PdfRectangle(72, 700, 300, 720), new PdfTextFieldOptions { MaxLength = 60, Required = true }); pdf.Form.AddCheckBox("terms", 0, new PdfRectangle(72, 660, 86, 674)); pdf.Form.AddRadioGroup("size", [(0, new PdfRectangle(72, 620, 86, 634), "S"), (0, new PdfRectangle(100, 620, 114, 634), "M")], selected: "S"); pdf.Form.AddComboBox("country", 0, new PdfRectangle(72, 580, 220, 596), ["Norway", "Sweden"]); pdf.Form.AddSignatureField("approval", 0, new PdfRectangle(72, 480, 272, 540)); pdf.Save("form.pdf"); Damaged and encrypted files Egap repairs what it can while reading: broken cross-reference tables, wrong lengths, bad page trees. Each repair adds a PdfWarning. With PdfReadOptions.Strict set, the first problem throws a PdfException instead. Encrypted files open with the user or owner password; RC4 and AES up to AES-256 are read and written. Saving By default a save appends only the changes to the original bytes (an incremental update), so signatures stay valid. A full rewrite writes a fresh, compact file: using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("in.pdf"); using PdfDocument other = PdfDocument.Open("other.pdf"); using PdfDocument merged = PdfDocument.Merge(pdf, other); // fields renamed on a clash, outlines appended merged.Save("merged.pdf", new PdfSaveOptions { Mode = PdfSaveMode.Rewrite, Compression = PdfCompression.Compact }); Recipes Short answers to common tasks in this area. Each one is complete: open, change, save. Merge files and keep some pages using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument cover = PdfDocument.Open("cover.pdf"); using PdfDocument report = PdfDocument.Open("report.pdf"); using PdfDocument merged = PdfDocument.Merge(cover, report); using PdfDocument chosen = merged.ExtractPages(PdfPageRange.Parse("1-3,5,z")); chosen.Save("merged.pdf");

articles/guides/flow-documents.html.title: Flow documents | Egap
articles/guides/flow-documents.html.summary: Flow documents Egap.Documents holds one editable document model for DOCX, plain text and, with the add-on packages Egap.Documents.Html and Egap.Documents.Markdown, HTML and Markdown: sections, paragraphs, runs, tables, lists, pictures, headers and footers, notes, fields, comments and tracked changes, with Word's style model. using Egap.Documents; Document doc = Document.Load("report.docx"); // any format Egap reads, told apart by content foreach (Paragraph p in doc.Descendants<Paragraph>()) { Console.WriteLine($"{p.ListLabel?.Text} {p.GetText()}"); // list labels computed as Word numbers them } DocumentBuilder builder = new(doc); // edit from code at a cursor builder.Writeln("Added at the end."); doc.Replace("colour", "color"); // also where the text crosses runs IReadOnlyList<TextMatch> found = doc.Find("color"); // paragraph, offset and text of each match doc.Save("report-edited.docx"); // what the model does not name is kept IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning> dropped = doc.Save("report.txt"); // the format from the extension, with what it left out DOCX to DOCX is lossless: what the model does not name travels along in each node's extension data. Saving to a format that cannot hold something, such as Markdown, returns a warning for each thing left out. Each format also reads as members of Document, which forward to the format's class with the same options and warnings: using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; Document report = Document.LoadDocx("report.docx"); report.SaveAsDocx("report-copy.docx"); string text = report.ToText(); // as TextFormat.ToText report.SaveAsPdf("report.pdf"); Document scanned = Document.LoadPdf("scanned.pdf"); // as PdfToDocument.Convert Document.Load and Save know DOCX, PDF, plain text and Docling JSON by themselves; HTML and Markdown join them once their add-on package is registered. Each format has its own page under Document formats, with its options and what it keeps. Text options Besides fonts, sizes and colours, runs take word spacing, an overline and any OpenType feature, such as ligatures, tabular or old-style figures and stylistic sets. Paragraphs choose where lines may break inside words. HTML's word-spacing, text-decoration: overline, font-feature-settings, font-variant-ligatures, font-variant-numeric, word-break and overflow-wrap read into the same settings. DOCX keeps the features Word has (ligatures, number forms and spacing, stylistic sets, contextual alternates); Word has no word spacing or overline. A justified paragraph can also stretch its Arabic lines with tatweels (kashida) between letters, as Word's low, medium and high kashida alignments do: set ParagraphFormat.Kashida to KashidaLevel.Low, Medium or High with ParagraphAlignment.Justify. What the tatweels do not take goes to word spaces, and lines in other scripts justify at spaces as before. In PDF exports the inserted tatweels are left out of the text, so copy and search give the words as typed. using Egap.Documents; Document doc = new(); DocumentBuilder builder = new(doc); builder.Font.WordSpacing = 2; builder.Font.Overline = true; builder.Font.Features = FontFeatures.Parse("liga=0, tnum"); builder.ParagraphFormat.WordBreak = WordBreak.Anywhere; builder.Writeln("Invoice 2026-118: https://example.com/a/very/long/address/that/must/break"); builder.ParagraphFormat.Bidi = true; builder.ParagraphFormat.Alignment = ParagraphAlignment.Justify; builder.ParagraphFormat.Kashida = KashidaLevel.Medium; builder.Writeln("تعلم اللغة العربية يفتح أبواب الأدب والعلوم والتاريخ للطلاب في كل مكان"); Barcodes InsertBarcode writes a barcode as a picture of the size you give. Layout and PDF export draw it as vectors; DOCX keeps it as an SVG picture with a PNG stand-in at 300 pixels per inch, as Word stores SVG pictures, so older readers show it too. Any SVG picture can carry such a stand-in in Picture.Fallback. using Egami.Barcodes; using Egap.Documents; Document label = new(); DocumentBuilder builder = new(label); builder.Writeln("Parcel 2026-118"); builder.InsertBarcode(Barcode.Code128("PARCEL-2026-118"), 200, 50); label.Save("label.docx"); Mail merge FillMergeFields fills a template's MERGEFIELD fields from one record. Each field becomes plain text in its own formatting, written with its number (\#), date (\@) and text (\*) formats and the text it puts before and after a value ( , ); IF fields that test the values are worked out. MergeData makes records from dictionaries, rows with column names and objects, without reflection that trimming would break. Implement IMergeData to read records from anywhere else. Fields the record has no value for are removed, each with a warning. using Egap.Documents; Document letter = Document.Load("letter.docx"); IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning> missing = letter.FillMergeFields(MergeData.From(new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["Name"] = "Kari Nordmann", ["Amount"] = 1234.5m, ["Due"] = new DateOnly(2026, 11, 1), })); letter.Save("letter-kari.docx"); A region repeats once per record of a sequence in the data: the rows or paragraphs from a TableStart:Lines merge field to a TableEnd:Lines one, or a table row whose fields are all named Lines.Something. Regions nest, and a field a line does not have is read from the record around it. MailMerge makes one document per record, as the sequence is read, and MailMergeAll one document of them all, each record starting on a new page (or as Separator says). using Egap.Documents; Document template = Document.Load("invoice-template.docx"); IEnumerable<IMergeData> customers = MergeData.From(["Name", "City"], [["Ola", "Oslo"], ["Kari", "Bergen"]]); int number = 1; foreach (Document invoice in template.MailMerge(customers)) { invoice.Save($"invoice-{number++}.docx"); } Document statements = template.MailMergeAll(customers, new MailMergeOptions { OnWarning = w => Console.WriteLine(w) }); Page layout Layout breaks the document into pages, with floats, columns, headers and footers, and footnotes. Each page draws onto any Egami canvas. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Layout; Document doc = Document.Load("report.docx"); DocumentLayout pages = doc.Layout(); // pages, lines and boxes linked to the model pages.Pages[0].Render(dpi: 150).Save("page1.png"); A group of blocks (a block content control) can say how it is placed across pages: kept together on one page, started on a new page when less than some height is left, never split, cut where the page ends, or drawn smaller to fit the room left. HTML's break-inside: avoid on a box of several blocks makes such a group. A paragraph can be clamped to a number of lines, ending in an ellipsis (HTML's -webkit-line-clamp); table rows marked as footer rows repeat at the bottom of each page the table continues from; and a section can balance its last page's columns. Word keeps the content, not these settings. using Egap.Documents; Document invoice = new(); DocumentBuilder builder = new(invoice); builder.Writeln("Lines of the invoice..."); ContentControl totals = builder.StartGroup(); totals.Paging = new GroupPaging { KeepTogether = true, EnsureSpace = 120 }; builder.Writeln("Subtotal: 1 200 NOK"); builder.Write("Total: 1 500 NOK"); builder.EndGroup(); Margin boxes put text in the page margins, as CSS's @page margin boxes do: a box in each corner and three along each edge, on every page of the section or only the first. They hold PAGE and NUMPAGES fields for page numbers and sit beside the headers and footers without moving the body. HTML's @top-left, @bottom-center and the other margin box rules read into them, counter(page) and counter(pages) included, and write back the same way. An element with position: running(name) leaves the body and shows in the boxes whose content is element(name). DOCX has no margin boxes, so the top and bottom ones are saved as a three-part table in the header or footer; the corner and side boxes are left out with a warning. using Egap.Documents; Document report = Document.Load("report.docx"); DocumentBuilder builder = new(report); builder.MoveToMarginBox(MarginBoxPosition.TopLeft); builder.Write("Quarterly report"); builder.MoveToMarginBox(MarginBoxPosition.BottomRight); builder.Write("Page "); builder.InsertField("PAGE"); builder.Write(" of "); builder.InsertField("NUMPAGES"); builder.MoveToMarginBox(MarginBoxPosition.TopLeft, firstPage: true); // an empty box: no title on the cover A table with a TableFormat.Position floats: it sits where its anchors and alignment or offsets put it (the text, the margins or the page), text after it wraps on the side with more room, and when it does not fit it goes on at the top of the next page's body with its header rows repeated. The text after a table that breaks follows it on the page where it ends, unless WordCompatibility.AllowTextAfterFloatingTableBreak is on; DoNotBreakWrappedTables keeps it on one page, and AllowOverlap = false moves it down until it clears the floating tables before it. A paragraph with a ParagraphFormat.Frame is an old-style Word frame: it and the paragraphs after it with the same frame are placed the same way and never split, and a frame with a DropCap is a large first letter that the next paragraph wraps beside. Floating tables and frames in table cells, headers, footers, notes and text boxes are laid out in the text. DOCX reads and writes both (w:tblpPr, w:tblOverlap, w:framePr), HTML reads float: left and float: right on a table as a floating table and writes it back, and a report table floats with Floating. using Egap.Documents; Document doc = new(); Body body = doc.AddSection().Body; Table facts = body.AddTable(3, 2); facts.Format.Position = new TablePosition { HorizontalAnchor = HorizontalAnchor.Margin, HorizontalAlignment = FloatingAlignment.End, // against the right margin VerticalAnchor = VerticalAnchor.Paragraph, // where the text after it starts DistanceLeft = 9, // the text keeps 9 points away }; body.AddParagraph("This text wraps beside the table on the left."); Paragraph cap = body.AddParagraph("O"); cap.Format.Frame = new FramePosition { DropCap = DropCap.Drop, DropCapLines = 3 }; body.AddParagraph("nce upon a time, the first letter of this paragraph sat three lines tall."); InsertTableOfContents writes a TOC field and builds its entries from the headings, each linked to its heading. Layout fills in the page numbers, as it does for every PAGEREF field. HTML's <nav data-toc> is read as such a field. using Egap.Documents; Document handbook = Document.Load("handbook.docx"); DocumentBuilder builder = new(handbook); builder.MoveToDocumentStart(); builder.InsertTableOfContents(); builder.InsertParagraph(); With Strict, layout throws a LayoutException naming the node and the page instead of degrading: a word too long for its column, a table or picture past the page, a character no font has, or a font with no stand-in. FontSettings.Portable uses only the document's embedded fonts and the bundled substitutes, never the system's, so a document prints the same on every machine; with a deterministic save the PDF bytes are the same too. Both suit documents your own code builds; for converting other people's files, leave them off and read the warnings. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Layout; Document report = Document.Load("report.docx"); try { DocumentLayout pages = report.Layout(new LayoutOptions { Strict = true, Fonts = FontSettings.Portable }); } catch (LayoutException e) { Console.WriteLine($"{e.Problem} on page {e.PageIndex + 1}: {e.Message}"); } Flex and grid layout A FlexContainer lays its items out in a row or a column, as CSS flexbox does: each item starts from its basis or its content's width, takes a share of the space left by its grow factor or gives some up by its shrink factor, and lines up along and across its line by the container's JustifyContent and AlignItems. With Wrap, items that do not fit go on the next line. A GridContainer places its items in columns and rows of tracks, as CSS grid does: tracks in points, per cent, fractions of what is left (fr) or sized to their content, items placed by line, span or named area, and the rest filled in by automatic placement. Pages break between a flex container's lines and between a grid's rows, and inside a line or row too tall for the room left; rows an item spans stay together. using Egap.Documents; Document invoice = new(); Body body = invoice.AddSection().Body; FlexContainer header = new(invoice) { Layout = new FlexLayout { JustifyContent = LayoutAlignment.SpaceBetween, ColumnGap = 12 } }; header.AddItem("Acme Ltd"); header.AddItem("Invoice 2026-118").Box = new BoxStyle { PaddingLeft = 6, Width = TableWidth.Points(160) }; body.Blocks.Add(header); GridContainer lines = new(invoice) { Layout = new GridLayout { Columns = [GridTrack.Fraction(1), GridTrack.Points(60), GridTrack.Points(80)], ColumnGap = 6, RowGap = 2 }, }; foreach (string cell in (string[])["Item", "Qty", "Price", "Paper", "2", "40 NOK"]) { lines.AddItem(cell); } GridItem total = lines.AddItem("Total: 80 NOK"); total.Column = 2; total.ColumnSpan = 2; body.Blocks.Add(lines); A BoxStyle draws a box around a container, an item or a group of blocks: margins, padding, borders, a background, rounded corners and a shadow, with a width and a least height. A group with a box breaks across pages like any other blocks; its box is drawn open where it breaks. Rounded corners and shadows draw on every Egami canvas; in a PDF a blurred shadow is drawn as an image. using Egap.Documents; Document letter = new(); ContentControl card = new(letter) { Box = BoxStyle.Padded(10).WithBorder(new Border(BorderStyle.Single, 1, DocumentColor.FromHex("336699"))) with { Background = DocumentColor.FromHex("F4F8FC"), CornerRadius = BoxCorners.All(6), Shadow = new BoxShadow(0, 2, 6) { Opacity = 0.3 }, MarginTop = 12, }, }; card.AddParagraph("Paid in full on 21 October."); letter.AddSection().Body.Blocks.Add(card); HTML's display: flex and display: grid read into these containers, with the properties listed on the HTML page; a box with border-radius or box-shadow becomes a group with a box. DOCX has no such containers, so a container is saved as a borderless table with its items in the cells, and a boxed group as a one-cell table; Word keeps the content and the cells' backgrounds, borders and padding, not the corners or the shadow. A text box can fit its text (FitToText), have its own insets (TextInsets), rounded corners (CornerRadius) and a shadow (Shadow). HTML's absolutely positioned and fixed boxes read as such text boxes, floating in front of the text. For PDF output, see PDF export and conversion.

articles/guides/fonts.html.title: Fonts | Egap
articles/guides/fonts.html.summary: Fonts Egap.Pdf and Egap.Documents use open fonts with the same glyph widths as the fonts documents name most. Text set in a substitute keeps the original's line breaks. Font in the document Substitute Helvetica, Arial Liberation Sans Times, Times New Roman Liberation Serif Courier, Courier New Liberation Mono Calibri Carlito Cambria Caladea Egap.Pdf and Egap.Documents use them on their own when a font is missing. You can also use them with Egami.Fonts directly: using Egami.Fonts; using Egami.Fonts.Substitutes; Typeface? arial = SubstituteFonts.Find("Arial", FontStyle.Normal); // Liberation Sans FontCollection all = SubstituteFonts.Collection; // every bundled face The fonts are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, and their licences ship in the package.

articles/guides/index.html.title: Guides | Egap
articles/guides/index.html.summary: Guides Each guide covers one area of Egap: what it does, the options and their defaults, and the limits. Some guides end with Recipes, short complete answers to common tasks such as merging files or adding page numbers, with code you can copy. The guides are grouped by package, and within a group they are in alphabetical order. Each document format has its own page in Document formats. If you are new, read Getting started first, and Packages to pick what to install. Egap.Pdf Reading, editing, rendering and saving PDF files. Editing PDF files: pages, metadata, outlines, annotations and forms; damaged and encrypted files; saving. Fonts: the open fonts that stand in for missing ones, in Egap.Pdf and Egap.Documents alike. OCR and searchable scans: making scanned PDFs searchable through an OCR engine you plug in. PDF tools: optimize, stamps and imposition, page ranges, compare and clean-up. Print production: preflight against a print profile, separations and ink coverage, colour conversion, PDF/X and overprint preview. Redaction and PDF/A: true redaction, replacing text, PDF/A and e-invoices. Rendering pages: pages to images, or onto any Egami canvas. Signatures: signing, verifying, and keys on smart cards and HSMs. Text, images and drawing: text extraction, finding text, images, and drawing on a page. Egap.Documents One document model for DOCX, HTML, Markdown and plain text, its page layout, and conversions to and from PDF. Flow documents: the document model, editing, text options, barcodes, mail merge and page layout. Moving to Egap.Documents 2.0: the new packages and namespaces, and what else changed. PDF export and conversion: documents to PDF, one-line conversions, and PDF back to documents. Reports in code: the fluent report API, with rows, tables, grids, styles, components and paging, and the live preview tool. Document formats The overview says what each format reads and writes, and how a file's format is found; then one page per format, with its options: Docling JSON DOCX EPUB, in the Egap.Documents.Html package HTML, in the Egap.Documents.Html package Markdown, in the Egap.Documents.Markdown package MHTML, in the Egap.Documents.Html package Plain text

articles/guides/migrating-to-2.0.html.title: Moving to Egap.Documents 2.0 | Egap
articles/guides/migrating-to-2.0.html.summary: Moving to Egap.Documents 2.0 Egap.Documents 2.0 is one converter package: it takes in everything Egap.Pdf.Conversion held, and HTML and Markdown move to two add-on packages. Most code compiles once the package references and the using lines change. Egap.Pdf does not change. Packages You used Use now Egap.Documents 1.x Egap.Documents 2.0 Egap.Pdf.Conversion Egap.Documents 2.0 (Egap.Pdf.Conversion is retired and gets no new version) HtmlFormat, HtmlLoadOptions, HtmlSaveOptions, PdfConvert.FromHtml, PdfStamp.Html, PageBand.Html Egap.Documents.Html 2.0 MarkdownFormat and its options, PdfConvert.FromMarkdown Egap.Documents.Markdown 2.0 dotnet remove package Egap.Pdf.Conversion dotnet add package Egap.Documents dotnet add package Egap.Documents.Html # if you read or write HTML dotnet add package Egap.Documents.Markdown # if you read or write Markdown Namespaces Type 1.x namespace 2.0 namespace PdfExport (SaveAsPdf, ToPdf), PdfExportOptions, PdfConvert, PdfConvertOptions, PageBand, PageMargins, TableOfContentsMode Egap.Pdf.Conversion Egap.Documents.Pdf PdfToDocument, PdfLayoutAnalyzer, PdfPageLayout and the Layout* types, PdfAutoTagger, TableCsv, HtmlStamp Egap.Pdf.Conversion Egap.Documents.Pdf DoclingJson, DoclingJsonOptions, DoclingImage, DoclingImageMode Egap.Pdf.Conversion Egap.Documents HtmlFormat, MarkdownFormat and their options Egap.Documents Egap.Documents (unchanged, now in the add-ons) Replace using Egap.Pdf.Conversion; with using Egap.Documents.Pdf;, and add using Egap.Documents; where you use the Docling types. Loading without naming the format Document.Load and Document.Save know DOCX, PDF, plain text and Docling JSON. They reach HTML and Markdown only after the add-on's Register(), called once at startup; PdfConvert.FromFile and HTML page bands use the same registration. Without it they throw a NotSupportedException that names the package and the call. using Egap.Documents; HtmlFormat.Register(); MarkdownFormat.Register(); Document notes = Document.Load("notes.md"); Calling HtmlFormat or MarkdownFormat directly, or PdfConvert.FromHtml and PdfConvert.FromMarkdown, needs no registration. Other changes A .txt file loads as plain text, one paragraph per line, instead of as Markdown. Document.Save("x.pdf") writes PDF. HtmlLoadOptions.Encoding is the fallback for bytes that name no encoding; it no longer overrides a meta charset. Each format also reads as members of Document, such as Document.LoadDocx, Document.LoadMarkdown, ToHtml and SaveAsDocx; the format classes' methods still work. The changelog lists every change under each package.

articles/guides/ocr.html.title: OCR and searchable scans | Egap
articles/guides/ocr.html.summary: OCR and searchable scans Egap makes scanned PDFs searchable through an OCR engine you plug in. It sends each page's image to the engine and writes the words that come back over the page as invisible text, so the page can be searched, selected and read aloud while it looks exactly as the scan. Egap ships no engine: use Egami's CommandOcrEngine for any program that writes hOCR or ALTO, such as Tesseract, or write a small class around an OS or cloud service (Egami's repository has samples for Tesseract, Windows OCR and Azure). Make a PDF searchable PdfOcr.MakeSearchableAsync changes the document in place; you save it. The report says, page by page, what was done, how many words were added and how long the engine took. using Egami.Ocr; using Egap.Pdf; using Egap.Pdf.Ocr; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("scan.pdf"); CommandOcrEngine tesseract = new("tesseract {image} {output} -l {langs} --dpi {dpi} hocr", new CommandOcrOptions { Output = OcrOutputFormat.Hocr }); PdfOcrReport report = await PdfOcr.MakeSearchableAsync(pdf, tesseract, new PdfOcrOptions { Languages = ["eng"], PdfA = PdfAConformance.PdfA2b, }); Console.WriteLine($"{report.Words} words on {report.Pages.Count(p => p.Status == PdfOcrPageStatus.Recognized)} pages"); pdf.Save("searchable.pdf"); A page that is one scanned image covering the page, at 150 dpi or more, is read as its own pixels, with no render and no resampling. Other pages are rendered at Dpi (300 by default). Each word is placed along its own baseline and scaled to its width, so selection follows rotated and skewed words. In a tagged document each word's language goes on its text. Option Default Does Mode Skip Skip leaves pages that have text alone; Redo removes an earlier invisible text layer and reads the page again, keeping visible text; Force reads every page, keeping its text Pages Every page The pages to look at, as indices from 0 Languages The engine's default The languages to read, as the engine names them Dpi 300 The resolution pages are rendered at when they are not one scanned image MinConfidence 0 Words the engine is less sure of are left out Deskew Off Straightens the image sent to the engine; the page itself is not changed RotatePages Off Turns a page the engine finds sideways or upside down, with its /Rotate MaxDegreeOfParallelism The processor count How many pages the engine reads at once; one at a time when the engine is not thread-safe Progress None Told how many pages are done StopOnError Off An engine error stops the run instead of marking the page as failed PdfA None A PDF/A level the document is converted to in the same pass AllowInvalidatingSignatures Off A signed document is refused unless this is set, since the text layer breaks its signatures MaxPages, MaxImagePixels 10,000 pages, 100 million pixels Limits for untrusted files; a larger scan is rendered, a larger render is made at a lower resolution Words the page already has as text are not added twice in Redo and Force. An image larger than the engine's MaxImageDimension is scaled down for it and the words scaled back. Scans in document conversion Document.LoadPdfAsync and PdfToDocument.ConvertAsync run scanned pages through PdfToDocumentOptions.OcrEngine, so their text becomes paragraphs rather than a picture. The PDF you pass is not changed. The sync LoadPdf keeps a scanned page as a picture with a warning. using Egami.Ocr; using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; CommandOcrEngine tesseract = new("tesseract {image} {output} --dpi {dpi} hocr", new CommandOcrOptions { Output = OcrOutputFormat.Hocr }); Document minutes = await Document.LoadPdfAsync("minutes-scan.pdf", new PdfToDocumentOptions { OcrEngine = tesseract }); minutes.Save("minutes.docx"); An existing hOCR or ALTO file When the OCR has already been run elsewhere, PdfOcrLayer.AddHocr and AddAlto add its words to a page, mapped onto the page's crop box; PdfOcrLayer.AddResult adds an engine's result through an image-to-page matrix you give.

articles/guides/pdf-export-and-conversio.title: PDF export and conversion | Egap
articles/guides/pdf-export-and-conversio.summary:
PDF export and conversion Egap.Documents saves documents as PDF and turns PDF pages back into documents, in namespace Egap.Documents.Pdf. HTML and Markdown come from their add-on packages, Egap.Documents.Html and Egap.Documents.Markdown, which add PdfConvert.FromHtml, PdfConvert.FromMarkdown, PdfStamp.Html and HTML page bands. Documents to PDF A document saves as PDF with its links, outline and, when asked, tags for accessibility. PDF/A works the same way. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Pdf; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; Document doc = Document.Load("report.docx"); doc.SaveAsPdf("report.pdf", new PdfExportOptions { Tagged = true, Conformance = PdfAConformance.PdfA2a }); Document page = HtmlFormat.Load("invoice.html"); page.SaveAsPdf("invoice.pdf"); With FormFields, HTML form controls and Word content controls become PDF form fields where they were laid out, each named by its HTML name or Word tag and starting with its value. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; Document form = HtmlFormat.Load("application.html"); form.SaveAsPdf("application.pdf", new PdfExportOptions { FormFields = true }); With Comments = PdfCommentMode.Annotations, the document's comments become PDF annotations any viewer shows and edits, as Acrobat writes them: a highlight over the text each is about (a note icon where it is about no text) with its author, date and text in a popup, replies threaded under it, and a resolved comment marked Completed. IncludeResolved = false leaves resolved comments out. The annotations print and have appearances, so PDF/A-2 and later hold, and tagged output puts each in an Annot element. Reading the PDF back gives the comments again, on the words they were about. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; Document draft = Document.Load("draft.docx"); draft.SaveAsPdf("draft-for-review.pdf", new PdfExportOptions { Comments = PdfCommentMode.Annotations, IncludeResolved = false }); One-line conversions PdfConvert turns HTML, Markdown, DOCX and images into PDF in one call. A page size and margins in the options replace the input's own. Converting a file reads its images from the file's own folder; HTML or Markdown given as text reads them only from BaseDirectory, and never from the network. FromFile handles HTML and Markdown files once their add-on is registered with HtmlFormat.Register() or MarkdownFormat.Register(). using Egap.Pdf; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; PdfConvert.FromFile("report.docx", "report.pdf"); PdfConvert.FromHtml("

Invoice

Total: 120 EUR

", "invoice.pdf", new PdfConvertOptions { PageSize = PdfPageSize.A4, Margins = PageMargins.All(Length.Mm(20)), Conformance = PdfAConformance.PdfA3b, }); using PdfDocument scans = PdfConvert.FromImages(["scan-1.jpg", "scan-2.png"], new PdfConvertOptions { PageSize = PdfPageSize.A4 }); scans.RenderPagesToFiles("thumbs/page-{page:00}.png", new PdfRenderOptions { Dpi = 72 }); Header and Footer put the same band on every page, in the top or bottom margin, in place of the input's own headers and footers. A text band has up to three parts (left, middle and right); an HTML band is styled with the page's own style sheets. Both take the placeholders {page}, {total-pages}, {label}, {date}, {time}, {title} and {file}, and a number format after a colon, as in {page:000}. HTML pages can set the same thing themselves with @page margin boxes and running elements (position: running(header) with content: element(header)). using Egap.Documents.Pdf; PdfConvert.FromHtml("Invoice 2026-118

Total: 120 EUR

", "invoice.pdf", new PdfConvertOptions { Header = PageBand.Html("
ACME {date}
"), Footer = PageBand.Text(left: "{title}", center: "Page {page} of {total-pages}") with { FontSize = 8 }, }); TableOfContents builds a table of contents from the headings, each entry linked to its heading, with or without page numbers. It goes where HTML has
or Markdown a [TOC] paragraph, else at the start. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; MarkdownFormat.Register(); PdfConvert.FromFile("handbook.md", "handbook.pdf", new PdfConvertOptions { TableOfContents = TableOfContentsMode.WithPageNumbers }); PdfStamp.Html lays out a piece of HTML as a stamp, such as a seal or a letterhead, and draws it on every page. using Egap.Pdf; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; using PdfDocument invoice = PdfDocument.Open("invoice.pdf"); invoice.Stamp(PdfStamp.Html("
PAID
", Length.Mm(50)) with { Anchor = StampAnchor.TopRight, Offset = new(-40, -40), Rotation = 15 }); invoice.Save("invoice-paid.pdf"); PDF to documents PdfToDocument analyses the pages into blocks, reading order, headings, lists, tables and figures, and builds a document you can save as DOCX, HTML or Markdown. Tagged PDFs, such as Word's, keep their tables' merged and nested cells. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Pdf; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("paper.pdf"); Document flow = PdfToDocument.Convert(pdf); flow.Save("paper.docx"); A hybrid PDF carries the editable document inside it. Export with PdfExportOptions.EmbedSource (or PdfConvertOptions.EmbedSource) and a DOCX of the document is attached as the PDF's source, an associated file marked /Source. Loading the PDF then gives that document back, styles and all, instead of analysing the pages. The copy is used only when it is marked as the source, is a DOCX, was embedded by Egap and the PDF has not been changed or signed since; otherwise the pages are analysed and a PdfToDocumentWarningKind.EmbeddedSourceSkipped warning says why. PdfToDocumentOptions.EmbeddedSource chooses Prefer (the default), Ignore or Require. PDF/A-1 and PDF/A-2 do not allow embedded files, so the export throws with them; PDF/A-3, PDF/A-4f and plain PDF carry the copy. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; using Egap.Pdf; Document report = Document.LoadDocx("report.docx"); report.SaveAsPdf("report.pdf", new PdfExportOptions { EmbedSource = true, Conformance = PdfAConformance.PdfA3b }); Document again = Document.LoadPdf("report.pdf"); // the DOCX inside, not an analysis of the pages Document pages = Document.LoadPdf("report.pdf", new PdfToDocumentOptions { EmbeddedSource = EmbeddedSource.Ignore }); The same analysis can tag an untagged PDF, write its layout as DoclingDocument JSON, or export its tables as CSV. A scanned page stays a picture unless you load with Document.LoadPdfAsync and an OCR engine (see OCR and searchable scans). Recipes Short answers to common tasks in this area. Each one is complete: open, change, save. Turn a Word file into an e-book using Egap.Documents; Document handbook = Document.LoadDocx("handbook.docx"); handbook.Properties.Title ??= "Staff handbook"; handbook.SaveAsEpub("handbook.epub", new EpubSaveOptions { NavigationDepth = 2 }); Each level 1 heading starts a chapter, and the headings make the book's table of contents. See EPUB. Print an e-book as PDF using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; Document book = Document.LoadEpub("novel.epub"); book.SaveAsPdf("novel.pdf", new PdfExportOptions { Outline = OutlineFrom.Headings }); Each chapter starts a new page, and the book's table of contents becomes the PDF's bookmarks. Save a page as one file using Egap.Documents; Document page = HtmlFormat.Load("offer.html", new HtmlLoadOptions { BaseUri = new Uri(new FileInfo("offer.html").FullName), ResourceResolver = uri => uri.IsFile && File.Exists(uri.LocalPath) ? File.ReadAllBytes(uri.LocalPath) : null, }); page.SaveAsMhtml("offer.mhtml"); The archive holds the page with its pictures, and opens in Chromium, Edge and Word. See MHTML.

articles/guides/pdf-tools.html.title: PDF tools | Egap
articles/guides/pdf-tools.html.summary: PDF tools Everyday tools for whole documents: compress, combine pages onto sheets, stamp, compare and clean up scans. Optimize Optimize makes a file smaller. The default, Lossless, keeps every pixel; the Print, Ebook and Screen presets downsample images and use JPEG. The report says what it saved. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument scan = PdfDocument.Open("scan.pdf"); IReadOnlyList<int> blank = scan.RemoveBlankPages(); // the page numbers removed scan.DeskewScannedPages(); PdfOptimizeReport smaller = scan.Optimize(PdfOptimizeOptions.Ebook with { JpegQuality = 70 }); Console.WriteLine($"{smaller.BytesBefore} -> {smaller.BytesAfter} bytes, {smaller.Images.Count} images changed"); scan.Save("scan-small.pdf"); // every save after Optimize is a compact rewrite Stamps and imposition Stamps are page numbers, headers and footers, Bates numbers, watermarks, text, images or whole pages. They are written as pagination artifacts, so a viewer or a later pass can tell them from the content. PdfImpose places pages onto sheets: N-up, booklets, posters, grids and fit to a page size. Text stamps fill placeholders per page: {page}, {total-pages} (or {pages}), {label}, {date}, {time}, {title} and {file}, with an optional format such as {page:000} or {date:yyyy-MM-dd}. PdfPlaceholders.Fill fills the same names in your own text. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument contract = PdfDocument.Open("contract.pdf"); contract.Stamp(PdfStamp.Text("Page {page} of {total-pages}") with { Anchor = StampAnchor.BottomCenter, Offset = new(0, 24) }); contract.Stamp(PdfStamp.Bates(new PdfBatesSequence("ACME-", digits: 6)) with { Anchor = StampAnchor.BottomRight }); using PdfDocument handout = PdfImpose.NUp(contract, new NUpOptions { Columns = 2, Rows = 2 }); handout.Save("handout.pdf"); PdfStamp.Barcode stamps any symbol Egami.Barcodes makes (QR, Data Matrix, PDF417, Aztec, Code 128, Code 39, ITF, EAN and UPC) as vector paths, so it scans at any zoom and in print. The draw options choose the quiet zone, bar width reduction and the font of the digits under a linear symbol. using Egami.Barcodes; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument invoice = PdfDocument.Open("invoice.pdf"); invoice.Stamp(PdfStamp.Barcode(Barcode.Qr("https://pay.example.com/2026-118"), 72, 72) with { Pages = [1], Anchor = StampAnchor.TopRight }); invoice.Stamp(PdfStamp.Barcode(Barcode.Code128("ORDER-118"), 160, 40) with { Anchor = StampAnchor.BottomLeft }); invoice.Save("invoice-coded.pdf"); Page ranges and units PdfPageRange.Parse reads pages written as text: numbers from 1, z for the last page, r2 for the second from the end, ranges such as 5-10 (or 10-5, backwards), :odd or :even after a part, and x before a part to leave its pages out. Length holds a size made from points, millimetres, centimetres or inches. It turns into points by itself, so it goes wherever a size in points is asked for. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument report = PdfDocument.Open("report.pdf"); using PdfDocument summary = report.ExtractPages(PdfPageRange.Parse("1-3,z")); report.Stamp(PdfStamp.Text("Draft") with { PageRange = PdfPageRange.Parse("2-z"), Offset = new(0, Length.Mm(10)) }); using PdfDocument handout = PdfImpose.NUp(report, new NUpOptions { Margin = Length.Mm(10), Gutter = Length.Mm(4) }); IReadOnlyList<int> evenPages = PdfPageRange.Parse("1-z:even").Resolve(report.Pages.Count); // 0-based indices Compare PdfCompare finds what changed between two versions, word by word with pages aligned, and also compares the rendered pages pixel by pixel. It can write a copy of the new document with each change marked. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument before = PdfDocument.Open("contract-v1.pdf"), after = PdfDocument.Open("contract-v2.pdf"); using PdfComparison changes = PdfCompare.Run(before, after); foreach (PdfTextChange change in changes.TextChanges) Console.WriteLine($"{change.Kind}: {change.OldText} -> {change.NewText}"); changes.WriteMarkup("contract-changes.pdf"); // the new document with each change marked Clean-up ConvertToGray turns every colour to gray, RemoveBlankPages drops empty pages, DeskewScannedPages straightens scans, and ConvertTextToOutlines turns text into paths so a file shows the same without its fonts. Recipes Short answers to common tasks in this area. Each one is complete: open, change, save. Add page numbers using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("report.pdf"); pdf.Stamp(PdfStamp.Text("Page {page} of {total-pages}") with { Anchor = StampAnchor.BottomCenter, Offset = new(0, Length.Mm(10)), PageRange = PdfPageRange.Parse("2-z"), // no number on the cover }); pdf.Save("report-numbered.pdf");

articles/guides/print-production.html.title: Print production | Egap
articles/guides/print-production.html.summary: Print production Check a PDF before it goes to a printer: what colours, profiles, inks and image resolutions it uses, and whether that fits the print job. Preflight PdfPreflight.Run lists what a document uses, page by page: output intents with their condition and profile, every colour space painted with (with its ICC profile description and spot ink names), images with their effective resolution where they are placed largest, fonts and whether they are embedded, transparency, overprint, hairlines, and each page's trim box and bleed. A device colour space that the page's resources replace with a Default space is reported as that space. Given a PdfPrintProfile, it also lists the issues that break it. Issues are the same PdfAIssue records as PDF/A checks use; preflight changes nothing, so none is fixable. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("brochure.pdf"); PdfPreflightReport report = PdfPreflight.Run(pdf, PdfPrintProfile.SheetfedCoated); foreach (PdfPreflightItem item in report.OutputIntents) { Console.WriteLine(item); // GTS_PDFX output intent FOGRA39 (Coated FOGRA39), CMYK profile "..." } foreach (PdfAIssue issue in report.Issues) { Console.WriteLine($"{issue.Clause} page {issue.Page}: {issue.Description}"); } Print profiles A PdfPrintProfile says what the job accepts. A value left null is not checked. Preset Max ink Min image dpi Colour spaces Bleed Thinnest rule PdfX4 150 all but DeviceRGB SheetfedCoated 330 % 250 CMYK, gray, spot 3 mm 0.25 pt WebOffset 300 % 200 CMYK, gray, spot 3 mm 0.25 pt Newspaper 240 % 150 CMYK, gray 0.3 pt Every preset requires embedded fonts and allows transparency. Images of one bit per pixel (line art) need twice the minimum resolution. Change any value with with: using Egap.Pdf; PdfPrintProfile vinyl = PdfPrintProfile.WebOffset with { Name = "Vinyl sleeve", MaxInkCoverage = 260, AllowTransparency = false }; Without a profile, Run only lists what the document uses. Strokes thinner than 0.25 pt (PdfPreflight.DefaultHairline) are then listed as hairlines. Separations and ink coverage RenderSeparations renders a page as ink plates: one gray raster per process ink of the press profile and one per spot ink the page uses. It draws with a true multi-ink renderer, so overprint, overprint mode, knockout and blend modes act on the inks as a press prints them. CMYK and gray go straight onto the process plates, Separation and DeviceN colourants onto their own plates, and RGB, Lab and calibrated colours convert through the press profile: the document's CMYK output intent, or FOGRA39 when it has none. using Egami; using Egami.Pixels; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("brochure.pdf"); using PdfSeparations plates = pdf.Pages[0].RenderSeparations(new PdfRenderOptions { Dpi = 150 }); foreach (PdfInkPlate plate in plates.Plates) { plate.Raster.Save($"{plate.Name}.png"); // 255 is full ink } Console.WriteLine($"max TAC {plates.MaxCoverage}%, {plates.ShareOver(300):P1} of the page over 300%"); using Raster<Rgba8> heat = plates.CoverageMap(limit: 300); // red where the ink is over the limit heat.Save("coverage.png"); PdfSeparationOptions picks another press profile, leaves some spot inks without a plate (DisabledSpots) or converts every spot to process (SpotsToProcess); a spot without a plate prints through its alternate colour. plates.Inks is the Egami InkRaster behind the plates, which saves a separated TIFF and makes a soft proof. When a print profile sets MaxInkCoverage, preflight separates every page at InkCoverageDpi (36 by default) and reports its most total ink and the share over the limit. Coverage is only reported: preflight does not change any colour. Colour conversion PdfColorConverter.Convert converts a document's colours into a print profile in place: RGB, calibrated, Lab and ICC-based colours go to the target, while CMYK and spot colours keep their numbers and plates. Vectors stay vectors. Colour operators, images, shadings, patterns, soft masks, Type 3 glyphs and annotation appearances are all converted; a JPEG photo stays a JPEG at the quality it had, and an Indexed image keeps its samples under a converted palette. using Egami.Colors; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("rgb.pdf"); PdfColorConversionResult result = PdfColorConverter.Convert(pdf, new PdfColorConversionOptions { Target = ColorProfile.Fogra39, // the default: the CMYK output intent, else FOGRA39 Spots = PdfSpotConversion.Keep, // Keep, Convert or ConvertAllButNamed BlackText = PdfBlackText.PureBlack, // black and gray text and thin rules on black ink alone }); Console.WriteLine(result); // what changed pdf.Save("cmyk.pdf"); Option Default What it does Target output intent, else FOGRA39 The gray, RGB or CMYK profile colours convert into Intent, BlackPointCompensation relative colorimetric, on How every conversion maps colours Spots Keep Spot colours keep their plates, with their alternate colours converted; Convert converts them too RetargetCmyk, SourceCmyk off Also convert CMYK from one press profile to another, such as coated to newspaper BlackText, ThinRuleWidth PureBlack, 0.5 pt Neutral text and rules up to the width go on black ink alone; images stay colorimetric Conversion does not limit ink: the target profile decides how much ink each colour takes, and preflight reports anything over a print profile's MaxInkCoverage. PDF/X PdfXConverter.Check checks a document against a PDF/X version and changes nothing; PdfXConverter.Convert fixes what it can in place and reports each fix. When a rule cannot be met, conversion changes nothing and the report says why. The reports are the same PdfAReport as for PDF/A. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("brochure.pdf"); PdfAReport report = PdfXConverter.Convert(pdf, PdfXConformance.PdfX4, new PdfXConvertOptions { OutputCondition = PdfOutputCondition.Fogra39, // the registered condition; its profile is embedded Bleed = 3, // millimetres past the trim box, where conversion sets the boxes }); if (report.Succeeded) { pdf.Save("print.pdf"); // written whole, unencrypted, as PDF 1.6 } else { Console.WriteLine(report); } Version Check Convert PDF/X-4, X-6 yes yes PDF/X-1a, X-3 yes when the file has no transparency (conversion does not flatten it) PDF/X-5n, X-6n yes with an n-colorant output condition, for content already in its inks PDF/X-4p, X-5g, X-5pg, X-6p yes no Conversion adds the output intent, sets a trim box (the crop box) and a bleed box where they are missing or wrong, writes the identification, title, dates and /Trapped, embeds fonts (from the machine, or bundled substitutes with AllowFontSubstitution), converts colours the output intent does not allow through PdfColorConverter, removes transfer functions, JavaScript and external content references, and flattens annotations that print inside the bleed box. PdfOutputCondition names registered print conditions: Fogra39 carries Egami's bundled profile; Fogra51, Fogra52, Gracol2013, Swop2013 and Newspaper need the profile from you with WithProfile. No open-source PDF/X validator exists; check important output in Acrobat Preflight or PackzView. Overprint preview SimulateOverprint renders a page as it prints: as ink plates, so overprint and spot colours act as on press, then proofed back to sRGB through the press profile, as Acrobat's Output Preview does. Without it, overprint is ignored, as viewers show pages on screen. using Egami; using Egami.Pixels; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("brochure.pdf"); using Raster<Rgba8> preview = pdf.Pages[0].Render(new PdfRenderOptions { Dpi = 150, SimulateOverprint = true }); preview.Save("as-printed.png");

articles/guides/redaction-and-pdfa.html.title: Redaction and PDF/A | Egap
articles/guides/redaction-and-pdfa.html.summary: Redaction and PDF/A Redaction Redaction removes the covered text, paths and image pixels from the file for real, then rewrites the whole file so nothing is left in older revisions. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("report.pdf"); pdf.Pages[0].Annotations.Add(new PdfRedactAnnotation(new PdfRectangle(72, 700, 300, 714))); pdf.ApplyRedactions(); // covered text, paths and pixels removed for real pdf.Save("redacted.pdf"); RedactText finds a phrase or a regular expression and redacts every match in one call; MarkRedactions only adds the marks, so they can be checked in a viewer before ApplyRedactions. ReplaceText swaps one text for another in the same font, size and colour. Where that font, often an embedded subset, has no glyph for a character of the new text, the match is left as it was with a warning, unless you give a fallback font. using Egap.Pdf; using Egami.Fonts; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("contract.pdf"); pdf.RedactText("Confidential", new PdfFindOptions { MatchCase = false }); PdfReplaceResult replaced = pdf.ReplaceText("2025", "2026", options: new PdfReplaceOptions { FallbackFont = Typeface.FromFile("NotoSans.ttf") }); foreach (PdfWarning warning in replaced.Warnings) { Console.WriteLine(warning.Message); // matches left as they were } pdf.Save("contract-2026.pdf"); Sanitize removes hidden data in one call: metadata, scripts, attachments, hidden layers, comments, form data, thumbnails and old revisions. PDF/A The converter keeps the file's objects, fixes what it can, and reports every fix. If a rule cannot be met it changes nothing and says why. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument archive = PdfDocument.Open("report.pdf"); PdfAReport conversion = PdfAConverter.Convert(archive, PdfAConformance.PdfA2u); if (conversion.Succeeded) { archive.Save("archive.pdf", new PdfSaveOptions { Linearize = true }); // linearized for fast web view } PDF/A-1b, 2a, 2b, 2u, 3a, 3b, 3u, 4 and 4f are written; levels 2a and 3a need a tagged file. Egap checks only the rules its writer and converter enforce, so use a validator such as veraPDF when conformance must be proven. E-invoices PdfInvoice.Embed turns a PDF into a Factur-X or ZUGFeRD e-invoice: it attaches the invoice's XML under its standard name with the relationship the standard asks for, converts the document to PDF/A-3 and writes the Factur-X schema into the XMP. The profile is read from the XML unless you give it. PdfInvoice.Read gives the XML back, with its standard and profile, and also reads ZUGFeRD 1.0 and 2.0 files. Egap does not write the XML itself; your invoicing system does. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("invoice.pdf"); PdfAReport report = PdfInvoice.Embed(pdf, File.ReadAllBytes("factur-x.xml")); pdf.Save("invoice-facturx.pdf"); using PdfDocument received = PdfDocument.Open("received.pdf"); if (PdfInvoice.Read(received) is PdfInvoice invoice) { Console.WriteLine($"{invoice.FileName}: {invoice.Profile}"); } received.Attachments.Add("data.csv", File.ReadAllBytes("data.csv"), PdfAttachmentRelationship.Data, "text/csv"); Recipes Short answers to common tasks in this area. Each one is complete: open, change, save. Redact a phrase using System.Text.RegularExpressions; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("statement.pdf"); pdf.RedactText("Ola Nordmann", new PdfFindOptions { MatchCase = false }); pdf.RedactText(new Regex(@"\b\d{11}\b")); // Norwegian national identity numbers pdf.Save("statement-redacted.pdf"); // written whole, so nothing redacted survives Turn an HTML invoice into a Factur-X PDF/A-3 using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; using Egap.Pdf; HtmlFormat.Register(); // once at startup: PdfConvert.FromFile reads .html using PdfDocument invoice = PdfConvert.FromFile("invoice.html", new PdfConvertOptions { PageSize = PdfPageSize.A4, Margins = PageMargins.All(Length.Mm(15)), }); PdfAReport report = PdfInvoice.Embed(invoice, File.ReadAllBytes("factur-x.xml")); // PDF/A-3b with the XML attached if (report.Succeeded) { invoice.Save("invoice-2026-118.pdf"); }

articles/guides/rendering.html.title: Rendering pages | Egap
articles/guides/rendering.html.summary: Rendering pages A page renders to an Egami raster, or onto any Egami canvas: pixels, SVG, or another PDF. using Egami; using Egami.Pixels; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("in.pdf"); using (Raster<Rgba8> image = pdf.Pages[0].Render(new PdfRenderOptions { Dpi = 150 })) { image.Save("page.png"); } using Raster<Rgba8> thumbnail = pdf.Pages[0].Render(PdfRenderOptions.FitTo(256, 256)); // decodes large images reduced PdfRenderOptions also picks the page box, a region, the background, which annotations and layers are drawn, and whether system fonts may stand in for fonts the file does not embed. Turn system fonts off for output that is the same on every machine. Fonts a file names but does not embed are drawn with bundled substitutes that keep the same widths. Pages render as on screen, where overprint is ignored. SimulateOverprint shows them as they print instead, and RenderSeparations gives the ink plates themselves; see Print production. Colour Device colours draw as the document's output intent says when it has one. Without a CMYK output intent, DeviceCMYK colours, CMYK JPEGs and spot colours with a CMYK alternate draw through the Coated FOGRA39 press profile, as on a European offset press. DefaultCmykProfile picks another press profile, such as one for U.S. web presses: using Egami.Colors; using Egap.Pdf; ColorProfile swop = ColorProfile.FromIcc(File.ReadAllBytes("USWebCoatedSWOP.icc")); PdfRenderOptions us = new() { DefaultCmykProfile = swop }; Transfer functions in a graphics state (/TR and /TR2) change the colours drawn after it, as they do on a printer. Set ApplyTransferFunctions to false to draw colours as they are.

articles/guides/reports.html.title: Reports in code | Egap
articles/guides/reports.html.summary: Reports in code Report.Create builds a document from code: pages with a header, a footer and content, and in them columns, rows, tables, grids, text, pictures, barcodes and form fields. It builds an ordinary Document, so the same report saves as PDF, DOCX or HTML and lays out with the same page flow as any other document. The types are in Egap.Documents.Reports. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Pdf; using Egap.Documents.Reports; using Egap.Pdf; (string Name, int Qty, decimal Price)[] lines = [("Paper", 2, 40m), ("Toner", 1, 590m)]; Document invoice = Report.Create(r => r .Title("Invoice 2026-118") .DefaultTextStyle(s => s.FontSize(10)) .Page(p => { p.Size(PdfPageSize.A4).Margins(Length.Mm(15)); p.Header().BorderBottom(1).Row(row => { row.Relative().Text("Acme Ltd").Style(s => s.FontSize(20).Bold()); row.Auto().AlignRight().Text("Invoice 2026-118"); }); p.Content().Column(col => { col.Spacing(8); col.Item().Text("Thank you for your order."); col.Item().Table(t => t .Columns(cols => cols.Relative(3).Fixed(40).Fixed(70)) .Lines(0.5) .Header("Item", "Qty", "Price") .Rows(lines, l => [l.Name, l.Qty, l.Price])); col.Item().KeepTogether().Background("F4F8FC").CornerRadius(6).Padding(8) .AlignRight().Text("Total: 670").Bold(); }); p.Footer().AlignCenter().Text(t => { t.Span("Page "); t.CurrentPageNumber(); t.Span(" of "); t.TotalPages(); }); })); invoice.SaveAsPdf("invoice.pdf"); invoice.Save("invoice.docx"); The page's Header(), Content() and Footer() each return the container to fill. Set the page's size, margins and text style before them: what goes into a container takes the settings in force when it was asked for. Containers Each place in a report is a Container. Settings come first and return the container: a box (Padding, Background, Border, BorderBottom, CornerRadius, Shadow, Width, MinHeight, MarginTop), the alignment of text inside (AlignLeft, AlignCenter, AlignRight, AlignJustify), a DefaultTextStyle, and paging (KeepTogether, EnsureSpace, ShowEntire, StopPaging, ScaleToFit). One element ends the chain; a container holds one, and Column puts several one under another. Element Builds Text("..."), Text(t => ...) A paragraph; spans with their own styles, page numbers, line breaks and links Image, Barcode A picture, held to the width there is unless a size is given; a barcode drawn as vectors Column Elements one under another, with Spacing between them Row A flex container: Fixed widths, Relative shares and Auto content widths side by side, as a table's columns are Grid A grid container: column tracks, spans and named areas Table A table: Columns, Header and Footer rows that repeat on every page, cells in order, Rows from data Line, PageBreak A rule across the width; a break to the next page TextField, CheckBox, DropDown Form controls that PDF export can turn into fields Component An IComponent, which composes itself into the container Page numbers are spans: CurrentPageNumber() and TotalPages() in Text(t => ...). Text is written as given, so {page} in data stays {page}. TextStyle and Container here are the report's own. Code that also uses Egami's text layout can name one with an alias, using ReportStyle = Egap.Documents.Reports.TextStyle;. Styles A TextStyle is immutable: each method returns a changed copy, so a style can be kept in a field and shared. What a style leaves unset comes from the text around it: the report's DefaultTextStyle, the page's, then the container's. A named style made with ReportBuilder.Style is also a character style in the document, so DOCX keeps it by name. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Reports; TextStyle note = TextStyle.Default.FontSize(8).Italic().FontColor("666666"); Document letter = Report.Create(r => r .Style("Strong", s => s.Bold().FontColor("993300")) .Page(p => p.Content().Column(col => { col.Item().Text("Payment is due within 14 days.").Style("Strong"); col.Item().Text("Prices include VAT.").Style(note); }))); Components A component is a class with a Compose method. It fills the container it is given, with any settings the caller put on it. using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Reports; Document report = Report.Create(r => r.Page(p => p.Content().Row(row => { row.Relative().Component(new AddressBlock("Acme Ltd", "Storgata 1, Oslo")); row.Relative().Component(new AddressBlock("Customer AS", "Kirkegata 9, Bergen")); }))); /// <summary>A name and a street in a thin box.</summary> sealed class AddressBlock(string name, string street) : IComponent { public void Compose(Container container) { container.Padding(4).Border(0.5).Column(col => { col.Item().Text(name).Bold(); col.Item().Text(street); }); } } Live preview The egap-preview dotnet tool shows documents on a local web page, drawn by Egap's own renderer, and shows them again when they change. ShowPreview() sends a document's pages to it; run the program under dotnet watch and the page follows each edit. Given a DOCX file instead, the tool draws the file again whenever it is saved. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, on port 12501 unless --port says otherwise, and ShowPreview() returns false when it is not running. It answers only requests addressed to 127.0.0.1 or localhost from programs and its own page, so other web pages can neither send it pages nor read the ones it shows. dotnet tool install -g Egap.Preview egap-preview # waits for ShowPreview() egap-preview letter.docx # or shows a file using Egap.Documents; using Egap.Documents.Reports; Document report = Report.Create(r => r.Page(p => p.Content().Text("Draft"))); report.ShowPreview(); // dotnet watch run: the page follows every edit HTML and Markdown are previewed from code, with the add-on that reads them: the tool itself only shows pages. To redraw an HTML template on every save, have dotnet watch watch it too, with <Watch Include="**/*.html" /> in an item group of the project file. using Egap.Documents; HtmlFormat.Register(); // Egap.Documents.Html Document invoice = Document.Load("invoice.html"); invoice.ShowPreview(); A strict layout that fails shows its message on the page, above the last pages that laid out, and is thrown as well. Strict layout and portable fonts A report's layout is strict and uses only portable fonts (Document.DefaultLayoutOptions): text that does not fit its column, a character no font has or a group that cannot be shown entire throws a LayoutException naming the node, and the report prints the same on every machine. Pass other LayoutOptions to Report.Create, or set DefaultLayoutOptions, to change that. DOCX keeps what Word can hold: rows and grids become borderless tables, and boxes become one-cell tables, without rounded corners or shadows. See Flex and grid layout.

articles/guides/signatures.html.title: Signatures | Egap
articles/guides/signatures.html.summary: Signatures Egap signs with .NET's own cryptography: PAdES baseline levels B-B to B-LTA, with approval and certification signatures, timestamps and visible appearances. Signing always writes to a new stream, as an incremental update. using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates; using Egap.Pdf; using HttpClient http = new(); using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("in.pdf"); using X509Certificate2 certificate = X509CertificateLoader.LoadPkcs12FromFile("me.pfx", "password"); await using (FileStream signed = File.Create("signed.pdf")) { await pdf.SignAsync("Signature1", new PdfSignOptions // PAdES, incremental, written to a new stream { Signer = PdfSigner.FromCertificate(certificate), Level = PadesLevel.BaselineT, Timestamp = new PdfTimestampClient(new Uri("https://tsa.example.com"), http), // Egap opens no connection itself }, signed); } Egap never opens a network connection on its own. Timestamps and revocation data come through the HttpClient you pass. Keys that live elsewhere (a smart card, an HSM, a cloud service) sign through any RSA or ECDsa object, or through deferred signing. Verifying using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates; using Egap.Pdf; X509Certificate2 root = X509CertificateLoader.LoadCertificateFromFile("root.cer"); using PdfDocument check = PdfDocument.Open("signed.pdf"); foreach (PdfSignature signature in check.Signatures) { PdfSignatureReport report = signature.Verify(new PdfVerifyOptions { TrustAnchors = [root] }); Console.WriteLine($"{signature.Name}: {report.Integrity} {report.Chain} {report.Timestamp} {report.ChangesSince}"); } The report gives a verdict for integrity, the certificate chain, revocation and the timestamp, and lists every change made after signing, each one rated allowed, suspicious or disallowed. Trust anchors always come from you. Smart cards and HSMs (PKCS#11) A key on a smart card, a USB token or an HSM is reached through its PKCS#11 library. Egap does not load native libraries, so the PKCS#11 calls come from a library you choose, such as Pkcs11Interop (Apache-2.0). Wrap the token's signing call in an RSA (or ECDsa) whose SignHash asks the token, and pass it to PdfSigner.FromKey with the certificate read from the token. The private key never leaves the device. using System.Security.Cryptography; using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates; using Egap.Pdf; // signOnToken stands for the PKCS#11 call: with Pkcs11Interop, session.Sign(new Mechanism(CKM.CKM_RSA_PKCS), key, digestInfo). Func<byte[], byte[]> signOnToken = digestInfo => throw new NotImplementedException("call the token here"); X509Certificate2 certificate = X509CertificateLoader.LoadCertificate(File.ReadAllBytes("token-certificate.cer")); using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("contract.pdf"); using RSA tokenKey = new TokenRsa(certificate, signOnToken); await using FileStream output = File.Create("contract-signed.pdf"); await pdf.SignAsync("Signature1", new PdfSignOptions { Signer = PdfSigner.FromKey(tokenKey, certificate) }, output); /// <summary>An RSA key whose private operation runs on a PKCS#11 token; it signs SHA-256 digests with PKCS#1 v1.5 padding.</summary> sealed class TokenRsa : RSA { // The DER prefix of a SHA-256 DigestInfo (RFC 8017 9.2), which CKM_RSA_PKCS expects in front of the digest. private static readonly byte[] Sha256Prefix = [0x30, 0x31, 0x30, 0x0d, 0x06, 0x09, 0x60, 0x86, 0x48, 0x01, 0x65, 0x03, 0x04, 0x02, 0x01, 0x05, 0x00, 0x04, 0x20]; private readonly X509Certificate2 certificate; private readonly Func<byte[], byte[]> signOnToken; public TokenRsa(X509Certificate2 certificate, Func<byte[], byte[]> signOnToken) { this.certificate = certificate; this.signOnToken = signOnToken; using RSA publicKey = certificate.GetRSAPublicKey()!; KeySizeValue = publicKey.KeySize; // the size of the signatures it makes LegalKeySizesValue = [new KeySizes(KeySizeValue, KeySizeValue, 0)]; } public override byte[] SignHash(byte[] hash, HashAlgorithmName hashAlgorithm, RSASignaturePadding padding) { if (hashAlgorithm != HashAlgorithmName.SHA256 || padding != RSASignaturePadding.Pkcs1) { throw new CryptographicException("The token signs SHA-256 with PKCS#1 v1.5 padding."); } return signOnToken([.. Sha256Prefix, .. hash]); } public override RSAParameters ExportParameters(bool includePrivateParameters) { using RSA publicKey = certificate.GetRSAPublicKey()!; return includePrivateParameters ? throw new CryptographicException("The private key stays on the token.") : publicKey.ExportParameters(false); } public override void ImportParameters(RSAParameters parameters) => throw new NotSupportedException(); } Egap signs with SHA-256 and PKCS#1 v1.5 padding by default, so this is all a token has to do. For a token reached over a network, or a signing service with its own API, deferred signing (PrepareSignatureAsync) hands out the bytes to sign and takes the signature back later. Recipes Short answers to common tasks in this area. Each one is complete: open, change, save. Sign a document using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("contract.pdf"); using X509Certificate2 certificate = X509CertificateLoader.LoadPkcs12FromFile("me.pfx", "password"); await using FileStream signed = File.Create("contract-signed.pdf"); await pdf.SignAsync("Signature1", new PdfSignOptions { Signer = PdfSigner.FromCertificate(certificate) }, signed); A key on a smart card or an HSM signs the same way, through an RSA that calls the device; see Smart cards and HSMs.

articles/guides/text-images-drawing.html.title: Text, images and drawing | Egap
articles/guides/text-images-drawing.html.summary: Text, images and drawing Each page gives its text in reading order and the images drawn on it. PdfCanvas is an Egami canvas whose drawing becomes PDF content, so anything you can draw with Egami.Drawing you can draw on a page. using Egami; using Egami.Drawing; using Egami.Pixels; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("in.pdf"); PdfPage page = pdf.Pages[0]; Console.WriteLine(page.ExtractText()); // lines in reading order foreach (PdfPlacedImage placed in page.GetImages()) // where each image is drawn, and its pixels { using Raster<Rgba8> pixels = placed.Image.ToRaster<Rgba8>(); } using (PdfCanvas canvas = new(page)) // Egami's canvas, drawn as PDF content over the page { canvas.FillRect(new RectF(72, 72, 200, 20), new SolidPaint(new RgbaF32(1, 0.9f, 0, 0.5f))); } pdf.Save("out.pdf"); The canvas works in points from the top left of the page as a viewer shows it. Text drawn on it embeds a subset of the font. What PDF cannot express exactly is drawn as an image, and each such fallback is counted in a warning. Find text FindText finds a phrase or a regular expression on every page, or on the pages a range chooses. Each match has its page, its text, its glyphs and one quadrilateral per line, so it can be highlighted or redacted. A phrase is found where it wraps onto the next line of a paragraph, and any white space in it matches any white space on the page. using System.Text.RegularExpressions; using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("contract.pdf"); foreach (PdfTextMatch match in pdf.FindText("Confidential", new PdfFindOptions { MatchCase = false, WholeWord = true })) { Console.WriteLine($"page {match.PageIndex + 1}: {match.Box}"); } IReadOnlyList<PdfTextMatch> ids = pdf.FindText(new Regex(@"\b\d{11}\b"), new PdfFindOptions { Pages = PdfPageRange.Parse("1-3") });

articles/packages.html.title: Packages | Egap
articles/packages.html.summary: Packages Package What it does Depends on Egap.Pdf Reads, edits, renders, signs, redacts and saves PDF; PDF/A, tagged PDF, optimize, imposition, stamps, barcodes, compare Egami.Drawing, Egami.Barcodes, Egami.Fonts.Substitutes Egap.Documents One document model with DOCX, plain text and Docling JSON, page layout onto any Egami canvas, PDF export, and PDF pages analysed and converted back into documents Egap.Pdf, Egami.Drawing, Egami.Barcodes, Egami.Svg, Egami.Metafiles, Egami.Fonts.Substitutes Egap.Documents.Html HTML and XHTML read and written through the CSS cascade, with @page rules and margin boxes, HTML to PDF, HTML stamps and page bands Egap.Documents, Egami.Css, AngleSharp Egap.Documents.Markdown CommonMark and GitHub Markdown read and written, with front matter and images, and Markdown to PDF Egap.Documents, Markdig Egap.Preview The egap-preview dotnet tool: a live preview of documents on a local web page Egap.Documents Egap.Cli The egap dotnet tool: convert, inspect, merge, split, stamp, redact, fill, sign and check PDFs from a shell, in pipelines and batches, and as an MCP server (guide) Egap.Pdf, Egap.Documents, the HTML and Markdown add-ons, System.CommandLine, ModelContextProtocol.Core Take Egap.Pdf alone for PDF work, Egap.Documents for documents and conversions, and an add-on for each of HTML and Markdown you read or write. The add-ons keep the class names you know (HtmlFormat, MarkdownFormat) in namespace Egap.Documents. Document.Load and Document.Save reach an add-on's format once you call its Register() at startup: using Egap.Documents; HtmlFormat.Register(); MarkdownFormat.Register(); Document notes = Document.Load("notes.md"); Without the call, loading such a file throws a NotSupportedException that names the package and the call. Document.Identify tells which format a file is in without any add-on. Each format's page under Document formats says which package it needs and what it reads and writes. The add-ons start at 2.0.0 and move in step with Egap.Documents. Egap.Pdf.Conversion is retired: its code is in Egap.Documents 2.0 (see Moving to Egap.Documents 2.0). Egami.Drawing brings in Egami and Egami.Fonts. Every package is fully managed, MIT-licensed, and targets .NET 10; the add-ons' parsers, AngleSharp (MIT) and Markdig (BSD-2-Clause), are managed too. The substitute fonts for missing fonts come from Egami.Fonts.Substitutes, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. All four packages are trimmable and work with Native AOT.

index.html.title: Egap | Egap
index.html.summary: Egap Egap is an open source family of document libraries for .NET 10: PDF files, and flow documents in DOCX, HTML and Markdown. It is a sister project to Egami, the 2D imaging library it draws with. MIT-licensed, with no strings for commercial use. Fully managed C#: no native binaries, no P/Invoke; images, fonts and drawing come from Egami, which is managed too. Safe on untrusted files: damaged files are repaired where possible, and every reader is fuzz-tested. PDF: read, edit, render, sign and verify, redact, PDF/A, tagged PDF, optimize, imposition, stamps and compare. Flow documents: one model for DOCX, HTML and Markdown (HTML and Markdown as add-on packages), with page layout, export to PDF and PDF converted back into documents. using Egap.Pdf; using PdfDocument pdf = PdfDocument.Open("in.pdf"); Console.WriteLine(pdf.Pages[0].ExtractText()); // lines in reading order pdf.Metadata.Title = "Quarterly report"; pdf.Outline.Add("Summary", PdfDestination.ToPage(pdf.Pages[0])); pdf.Save("out.pdf"); // incremental: the original bytes plus the changes Start with Getting started, browse the guides and the document formats, or look anything up in the API reference.
